def to_homogeneous(
    self,
    node_attrs: Optional[list[str]] = None,
    edge_attrs: Optional[list[str]] = None,
    add_node_type: bool = True,
    add_edge_type: bool = True,
    dummy_values: bool = True,
) -> GraphData:
    """Converts the heterogeneous graph to a homogeneous :class:`GraphData`,
    as PyG's ``HeteroData.to_homogeneous()``.

    Nodes are stacked by node type in the order of :attr:`node_types`, and
    the edges of every edge type (in the order of :attr:`edge_types`) are
    offset accordingly and concatenated.

    Per-type attributes are the dict attributes named ``<name>_dict`` whose
    keys are node types (e.g. ``node_features_dict``,
    ``node_labels_dict``, ``train_mask_dict``) or edge types (e.g.
    ``edge_features_dict``). They are merged into a single ``<name>``
    attribute (e.g. ``node_features``) if every type has them with the
    same number of dimensions and the same shape beyond the first one
    (2D node attributes of different widths are zero-padded to the widest
    one). With ``dummy_values``, types missing an attribute are first
    filled with ``NaN`` (floats), ``False`` (booleans) or ``-1``
    (integers), provided the types that have it agree on its shape.

    If ``edge_labels_index_dict`` is set, ``edge_labels_dict`` is aligned
    with it rather than with the edges: both are then offset and
    concatenated into ``edge_labels_index`` and ``edge_labels``.
    Graph-level attributes (e.g. ``graph_labels``) are copied as they are,
    and the other dict attributes are dropped.

    Args:
        node_attrs: Names (without ``_dict``) of the node attributes to
            merge. All mergeable ones if ``None``. Default: ``None``
        edge_attrs: Names (without ``_dict``) of the edge attributes to
            merge. All mergeable ones if ``None``. Default: ``None``
        add_node_type: Whether to add a ``node_type`` array holding the
            index of the type of each node in :attr:`node_types`.
            Default: ``True``
        add_edge_type: Whether to add an ``edge_type`` array holding the
            index of the type of each edge in :attr:`edge_types`.
            Default: ``True``
        dummy_values: Whether to fill missing attributes with dummy
            values. Default: ``True``

    Returns:
        The homogeneous graph, with an explicit ``num_nodes``.

    Example:

    .. code-block:: python

        data = HeteroGraphData(
            edge_index_dict={
                ("user", "rates", "movie"): mx.array([[0, 1], [0, 1]]),
            },
            node_features_dict={
                "user": mx.array([[0.2], [0.8]]),
                "movie": mx.array([[0.5], [0.3]]),
            },
        )
        graph = data.to_homogeneous()
        graph.edge_index
        # mx.array([[0, 1], [2, 3]])
        graph.node_type
        # mx.array([0, 0, 1, 1])
    """
    node_types, edge_types = self.metadata()
    num_nodes_dict = self.num_nodes
    offsets, total = {}, 0
    for node_type in node_types:
        offsets[node_type] = total
        total += num_nodes_dict[node_type]
    num_edges_dict = self.num_edges

    node_dicts, edge_dicts = self._typed_attributes()
    if self.edge_labels_index_dict:
        edge_dicts.pop("edge_labels", None)

    def merge(
        dicts: dict[str, dict],
        types: list,
        sizes: dict,
        keys: Optional[list[str]],
        pad_2d: bool,
    ) -> dict[str, mx.array]:
        merged = {}
        for name, values in dicts.items():
            if keys is not None and name not in keys:
                continue
            trailing = {tuple(v.shape[1:]) for v in values.values()}
            ndims = {v.ndim for v in values.values()}
            if len(values) < len(types):
                if not dummy_values or len(trailing) != 1:
                    continue
                ref = next(iter(values.values()))
                if mx.issubdtype(ref.dtype, mx.floating):
                    dummy: Any = float("nan")
                elif ref.dtype == mx.bool_:
                    dummy = False
                else:
                    dummy = -1
                values = {
                    t: values.get(t)
                    if t in values
                    else mx.full((sizes[t], *ref.shape[1:]), dummy, ref.dtype)
                    for t in types
                }
            if len(ndims) != 1:
                continue
            arrays = [values[t] for t in types]
            if len(trailing) != 1:
                if not (pad_2d and ndims == {2}):
                    continue
                width = max(a.shape[1] for a in arrays)
                arrays = [
                    mx.pad(a, [(0, 0), (0, width - a.shape[1])]) for a in arrays
                ]
            merged[name] = mx.concatenate(arrays, axis=0)
        return merged

    attributes: dict[str, Any] = {}
    handled = {f"{name}_dict" for name in (*node_dicts, *edge_dicts)}
    handled |= {"edge_index_dict", "edge_labels_index_dict", "num_nodes_dict"}
    if self.edge_labels_index_dict:
        handled.add("edge_labels_dict")
    for key, value in vars(self).items():
        if key in handled or key.startswith("_"):
            continue
        # Other dicts cannot be merged nor batched as graph attributes.
        if value is not None and not isinstance(value, dict):
            attributes[key] = value

    attributes.update(
        merge(node_dicts, node_types, num_nodes_dict, node_attrs, pad_2d=True)
    )
    attributes.update(
        merge(edge_dicts, edge_types, num_edges_dict, edge_attrs, pad_2d=False)
    )

    def offset(edge_type: tuple, edge_index: mx.array) -> mx.array:
        src, _, dst = edge_type
        shift = mx.array([[offsets[src]], [offsets[dst]]], dtype=edge_index.dtype)
        return edge_index + shift

    if len(edge_types) > 0:
        edge_index = mx.concatenate(
            [offset(et, self.edge_index_dict[et]) for et in edge_types], axis=1
        )
    else:
        edge_index = mx.zeros((2, 0), dtype=mx.int32)

    if self.edge_labels_index_dict:
        label_types = list(self.edge_labels_index_dict.keys())
        attributes["edge_labels_index"] = mx.concatenate(
            [offset(et, self.edge_labels_index_dict[et]) for et in label_types],
            axis=1,
        )
        labels = self.edge_labels_dict or {}
        if all(et in labels for et in label_types):
            attributes["edge_labels"] = mx.concatenate(
                [labels[et] for et in label_types], axis=0
            )

    if add_node_type:
        attributes["node_type"] = mx.array(
            np.repeat(
                np.arange(len(node_types)),
                [num_nodes_dict[t] for t in node_types],
            ).astype(np.int32)
        )
    if add_edge_type:
        attributes["edge_type"] = mx.array(
            np.repeat(
                np.arange(len(edge_types)),
                [num_edges_dict[t] for t in edge_types],
            ).astype(np.int32)
        )

    graph = GraphData(edge_index=edge_index, **attributes)
    graph.num_nodes = total
    return graph

def to_csc_dict(
    self,
) -> tuple[dict[Any, mx.array], dict[Any, mx.array], dict[Any, mx.array]]:
    """Converts every edge type to CSC format (edges grouped by destination).

    This is the input format of ``mlx_cluster.hetero_neighbor_sample``.

    Returns:
        A tuple ``(colptr_dict, row_dict, perm_dict)``, each keyed by edge
        type ``(src, rel, dst)``:

        - ``colptr_dict[et]``: ``int64`` array of length ``num_dst_nodes + 1``;
            the incoming edges of destination node ``v`` are at positions
            ``colptr[v]`` to ``colptr[v + 1]``.
        - ``row_dict[et]``: ``int64`` source node of each edge, in CSC order.
        - ``perm_dict[et]``: ``int64`` original position (column in
            ``edge_index_dict[et]``) of each edge in CSC order, used to look up
            edge features of sampled edges.
    """
    num_nodes = self.num_nodes
    colptr_dict, row_dict, perm_dict = {}, {}, {}
    for edge_type, edge_index in self.edge_index_dict.items():
        src_node_type, _, dst_node_type = edge_type
        src = np.asarray(edge_index[0]).astype(np.int64)
        dst = np.asarray(edge_index[1]).astype(np.int64)
        n_src = num_nodes[src_node_type]
        n_dst = num_nodes[dst_node_type]
        if src.size > 0 and (src.min() < 0 or src.max() >= n_src):
            raise ValueError(
                f"Edge type {edge_type} has source ids outside [0, {n_src}) "
                f"for node type '{src_node_type}'"
            )
        if dst.size > 0 and (dst.min() < 0 or dst.max() >= n_dst):
            raise ValueError(
                f"Edge type {edge_type} has destination ids outside [0, {n_dst}) "
                f"for node type '{dst_node_type}'"
            )

        order = np.argsort(dst, kind="stable")
        colptr = np.zeros(n_dst + 1, dtype=np.int64)
        np.cumsum(np.bincount(dst, minlength=n_dst), out=colptr[1:])

        colptr_dict[edge_type] = mx.array(colptr)
        row_dict[edge_type] = mx.array(src[order])
        perm_dict[edge_type] = mx.array(order.astype(np.int64))
    return colptr_dict, row_dict, perm_dict

def has_isolated_nodes(self, node_type: str) -> bool:
    """Returns a boolean of whether the graph has isolated nodes of the
    given type
    (i.e., nodes that don't have a link to any other nodes)"""
    num_nodes = self.num_nodes[node_type]
    for edge_type, edge_index in self.edge_index_dict.items():
        src_node_type, _, dst_node_type = edge_type
        if src_node_type == node_type or dst_node_type == node_type:
            if has_isolated_nodes(edge_index, num_nodes):
                return True
    return False

items.title: MemmapFeatureStore
items.text:
MemmapFeatureStore(root: str, num_threads: int = 8)

Bases: FeatureStore

A FeatureStore keeping every array in a .npy file on disk.

Only the rows that are asked for are read, so the arrays (e.g. node features of a large graph) can be larger than the memory. Rows given as an index array are read with positional reads (os.preadv), in increasing order and spread over num_threads threads: nearby rows (less than 64 KB apart) are read with one request, isolated rows one by one. The process only holds the requested rows (plus at most 16 MB per thread for gaps), without the read-ahead and resident pages of a memory mapping (the OS may still keep the file in its cache). Other reads (all rows, slices) and writes go through np.memmap.

Arrays are stored as <root>/<group_name or "_">/<attr_name>.npy. Large arrays can be written in chunks without holding them in memory, with create_tensor():

from mlx_graphs.data import MemmapFeatureStore

store = MemmapFeatureStore("features/")
x = store.create_tensor("x", shape=(num_nodes, 512), dtype="float32")
for start in range(0, num_nodes, 100_000):
    x[start : start + 100_000] = compute_features(start)
x.flush()
del x

store.get_tensor(attr_name="x", index=mx.array([3, 1, 4]))

@classmethod
def from_data(
    cls, data: Any, root: str, attrs: Optional[list[str]] = None
) -> "MemmapFeatureStore":
    """Writes the array attributes of a
    :class:`~mlx_graphs.data.GraphData` (all but ``edge_index`` unless
    ``attrs`` lists the ones to keep) to a new store in ``root``."""
    store = cls(root)
    for name, value in _graph_arrays(data, attrs).items():
        store.put_tensor(value, attr_name=name)
    return store

Source code in mlx_graphs/data/feature_store.py 
def create_tensor(
    self,
    attr_name: str,
    shape: tuple[int, ...],
    dtype: Any = "float32",
    group_name: Optional[str] = None,
) -> np.memmap:
    """Creates an array on disk and returns it as a writable
    ``np.memmap``, to be filled in chunks (call ``flush()`` and drop it
    when done)."""
    attr = TensorAttr(group_name, attr_name)
    path = self._path(attr)
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(path), exist_ok=True)
    out = np.lib.format.open_memmap(
        path, mode="w+", dtype=np.dtype(dtype), shape=tuple(shape)
    )
    self._register(attr)
    return out

items.title: MemmapGraphStore
items.text:
MemmapGraphStore(root: str)

Bases: GraphStore

A GraphStore keeping its edges in .npy files, read through memory mapping, so that a graph converted once (e.g. to CSC) can be reopened instantly, without parsing or sorting its edges again.

Only homogeneous graphs (edge_type=None) and string edge types are supported. Files are <root>/<edge_type or "_">.{0,1}.npy plus a <root>/edges.json index.

Example:

from mlx_graphs.data import MemmapGraphStore

store = MemmapGraphStore("graph/")
colptr, row, perm = InMemoryGraphStore.from_data(data).csc()
store.put_edge_index((row, colptr), layout="csc", size=(n, n))

# later, in another process
store = MemmapGraphStore("graph/")
colptr, row, _ = store.csc()

TemporalData(
    src: Optional[array] = None,
    dst: Optional[array] = None,
    t: Optional[array] = None,
    msg: Optional[array] = None,
    **kwargs,
)

A stream of events describing a temporal graph (a Continuous-Time Dynamic Graph), as PyG's torch_geometric.data.TemporalData.

Each event i is a (temporal) edge from the source node src[i] to the destination node dst[i] at time t[i], with a message (event features) msg[i]. Any other per-event attribute (e.g. labels y) can be passed to the constructor or set afterwards.

Indexing with a string returns an attribute (events["src"]); any other index (an integer, a slice, a list, an integer array or a boolean mask) selects events and returns a new TemporalData in which every array whose first dimension is num_events is indexed, as in PyG.

def index_select(
    self, idx: Union[int, slice, Sequence[int], np.ndarray, mx.array]
) -> "TemporalData":
    """Selects events.

    Every array attribute whose first dimension is ``num_events`` is
    indexed; the others are kept as they are.

    Args:
        idx: An integer (kept as a one-event selection), a slice, a list or
            array of event positions, or a boolean mask over the events

    Returns:
        A new :class:`TemporalData` with the selected events.
    """
    num_events = self.num_events
    idx = _prepare_index(idx, num_events)
    out = copy.copy(self)
    for key, value in self._store.items():
        if (
            isinstance(value, mx.array)
            and value.ndim > 0
            and value.shape[0] == num_events
        ):
            out._store[key] = value[idx]
    return out

def train_val_test_split(
    self, val_ratio: float = 0.15, test_ratio: float = 0.15
) -> tuple["TemporalData", "TemporalData", "TemporalData"]:
    """Splits the events into training, validation and test sets according to
    time, as in PyG.

    The split times are the ``1 - val_ratio - test_ratio`` and
    ``1 - test_ratio`` quantiles of ``t``, and events are assumed to be
    sorted by time.

    Args:
        val_ratio: Proportion of events in the validation set. Default:
            ``0.15``
        test_ratio: Proportion of events in the test set. Default: ``0.15``

    Returns:
        The training, validation and test events.
    """
    t = _to_numpy(self.t)
    val_time, test_time = np.quantile(
        t, [1.0 - val_ratio - test_ratio, 1.0 - test_ratio]
    )
    val_idx = int((t <= val_time).sum())
    test_idx = int((t <= test_time).sum())
    return self[:val_idx], self[val_idx:test_idx], self[test_idx:]

Source code in mlx_graphs/data/temporal.py 
def __inc__(self, key: str, *args, **kwargs) -> Optional[int]:
    """Increment applied to ``key`` when batching: ``num_nodes`` for
    ``src`` and ``dst``, ``max + 1`` for attributes containing ``"batch"``,
    and no increment otherwise (as PyG)."""
    value = self._store.get(key)
    if "batch" in key and isinstance(value, mx.array):
        return int(value.max().item()) + 1 if value.size > 0 else 0
    if key in ("src", "dst"):
        return self.num_nodes
    return None

@classmethod
def from_data_list(cls, data_list: Sequence["TemporalData"]) -> "TemporalData":
    """Concatenates several event streams into one, as PyG's
    ``Batch.from_data_list`` does for ``TemporalData``.

    ``src`` and ``dst`` of each stream are offset by the number of nodes of
    the previous streams (see :meth:`__inc__`), attributes containing
    ``"batch"`` by their number of groups, and all the other array
    attributes are concatenated as they are. Non-array attributes become
    lists.

    Args:
        data_list: The event streams, with the same attributes

    Returns:
        The concatenated events.
    """
    if len(data_list) == 0:
        raise ValueError("Cannot batch an empty list of TemporalData")
    first = data_list[0]
    out = cls()
    for key in first.keys():
        values = [data[key] for data in data_list]
        if not all(isinstance(v, mx.array) for v in values):
            out[key] = values
            continue
        cat_dim = first.__cat_dim__(key)
        if first.__inc__(key) is not None:
            incs = np.cumsum([0] + [data.__inc__(key) for data in data_list])
            values = [v + int(inc) for v, inc in zip(values, incs[:-1])]
        out[key] = mx.concatenate(values, axis=cat_dim)
    return out

@classmethod
def cast(cls, *args: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> "TensorAttr":
    """A :class:`TensorAttr` from another one, a tuple
    ``(group_name, attr_name[, index])`` or keyword arguments."""
    if len(args) == 1 and not kwargs:
        value = args[0]
        if isinstance(value, TensorAttr):
            return value
        if isinstance(value, tuple):
            return cls(*value)
        if isinstance(value, dict):
            return cls(**value)
    return cls(*args, **kwargs)

@validate_list_of_graph_data
def collate(graph_list: list[GraphData]) -> dict:
    """Concatenates attributes of multiple graphs based on the specifications
    of each `GraphData`.

    By default, concatenates all default array attributes in dim 0
    apart from `edge_index` which is concatenated along dim 1.
    Each graph remains independent in the final graph by incrementing
    the indices in `edge_index` based on the cumsum of previous number
    of nodes per graph.

    Args:
        graph_list: List of `GraphData` objects to collate

    Returns:
        Dict containing all the attributes of the unified and disconnected big graph as
        well as the "private" attributes used behind the hood by the batching.
        These private attributes start with an underscore "_" and can be ignore by
        the user.
    """
    batch_attr_dict = {}
    first_graph = graph_list[0]

    # `_num_nodes` is a scalar node count, not an array to concatenate.
    # It is handled separately at the end.
    attributes = [attr for attr in first_graph.to_dict() if attr != "_num_nodes"]

    # Offsets of incremented attributes (e.g. `edge_index`) only depend on the
    # value returned by `__inc__`, usually the number of nodes, so graphs are
    # only asked once per distinct attribute.
    for attr in attributes:
        arrays = [getattr(graph, attr) for graph in graph_list]

        # Non-array attributes, as in PyG: Python / numpy scalars (e.g. the
        # `batch_size` of NeighborLoader subgraphs) become an array with one
        # entry per graph, anything else (strings, ...) a list. Unbatching gives
        # each graph its original value back.
        # NumPy scalars have a `shape` too, but cannot be concatenated.
        if not all(isinstance(value, (mx.array, np.ndarray)) for value in arrays):
            if all(isinstance(value, _SCALAR_TYPES) for value in arrays):
                batch_attr_dict[attr] = mx.array(np.asarray(arrays))
                batch_attr_dict[f"_scalar_{attr}"] = True
            else:
                batch_attr_dict[attr] = arrays
                batch_attr_dict[f"_list_{attr}"] = True
            continue

        cat_dim = first_graph.__cat_dim__(key=attr)
        increment = first_graph.__inc__(key=attr)
        # 0-dim arrays are stacked into one entry per graph, as in PyG, and
        # unbatched back to 0-dim arrays.
        if all(array.ndim == 0 for array in arrays):
            arrays = [array.reshape(1) for array in arrays]
            cat_dim = 0
            batch_attr_dict[f"_stack_{attr}"] = True
        sizes = [array.shape[cat_dim] for array in arrays]
        batched = mx.concatenate(arrays, axis=cat_dim)

        # `None` means no increment; 0 (e.g. a first graph without nodes)
        # still needs the offsets of the following graphs.
        if increment is not None:
            increments = [graph.__inc__(attr) for graph in graph_list]
            cumsum = np.zeros(len(graph_list) + 1, dtype=np.int64)
            np.cumsum(increments, out=cumsum[1:])

            # One offset per element along the concatenation axis, added in a
            # single operation instead of one addition per graph.
            offsets = np.repeat(cumsum[:-1], sizes)
            shape = [1] * batched.ndim
            shape[cat_dim] = -1
            batched = batched + mx.array(offsets, dtype=batched.dtype).reshape(shape)

            batch_attr_dict[f"_inc_{attr}"] = True
            batch_attr_dict[f"_cumsum_{attr}"] = mx.array(cumsum)

            if attr == "edge_index":
                batch_indices = np.repeat(np.arange(len(graph_list)), increments)
                batch_attr_dict["_batch_indices"] = mx.array(
                    batch_indices.astype(np.int32)
                )

        batch_attr_dict[attr] = batched
        batch_attr_dict[f"_size_{attr}"] = mx.array(sizes)
        batch_attr_dict[f"_cat_dim_{attr}"] = cat_dim

    # Keep explicit node counts so the batch reports the right total and each
    # graph gets its own count back when unbatching.
    if "_num_nodes" in graph_list[0].to_dict():
        num_nodes_list = [graph.num_nodes for graph in graph_list]
        batch_attr_dict["_num_nodes"] = sum(num_nodes_list)
        batch_attr_dict["_num_nodes_per_graph"] = mx.array(num_nodes_list)

    return batch_attr_dict

Decorator function to check the validity of a list of GraphData.

Source code in mlx_graphs/data/utils.py 
def validate_list_of_graph_data(func):
    """Decorator function to check the validity of a list of `GraphData`."""

    @functools.wraps(func)
    def wrapper(graph_list: list[GraphData], *args, **kwargs):
        if not isinstance(graph_list, list):
            raise ValueError(f"Expected list of GraphData, got {type(graph_list)}.")
        try:
            expected_attr = set(graph_list[0].to_dict())
        except AttributeError:
            raise ValueError(
                "Expected list of GraphData. "
                "Graph at index 0 in the batch is not of type `GraphData`."
            )
        for i, graph in enumerate(graph_list):
            if not isinstance(graph, GraphData):
                raise ValueError(
                    "Expected list of GraphData. "
                    f"Graph at index {i} in the batch is not of type `GraphData`."
                )
            graph_attr = set(graph.to_dict())
            if graph_attr != expected_attr:
                raise ValueError(
                    "A graph in the batch has mismatching attributes. "
                    f"Found attributes at graph index {i}: {graph_attr}."
                )

        return func(graph_list, *args, **kwargs)

    return wrapper

Bases: _GeomGCNDataset

The actor-only induced subgraph of the film-director-actor-writer network used in the "Geom-GCN: Geometric Graph Convolutional Networks" paper.

Each node corresponds to an actor, and the edge between two nodes denotes co-occurrence on the same Wikipedia page. Node features correspond to some keywords in the Wikipedia pages. The task is to classify the nodes into five categories in terms of words of the actor's Wikipedia page.

The graph has 7,600 nodes, 30,019 edges, 932 features and 5 classes. The 10 fixed train/validation/test splits (60%/20%/20%) of the Geom-GCN paper are stored as masks of shape [num_nodes, 10] in the train_mask, val_mask and test_mask attributes.

This dataset follows the implementation of PyG.

DBLP is a heterogeneous graph containing four types of entities - authors (4,057 nodes), papers (14,328 nodes), terms (7,723 nodes), and conferences (20 nodes). def index_select(
    self, idx: Union[slice, mx.array, np.ndarray, Sequence]
) -> "Dataset":
    """Returns a new dataset with the graphs at the indices ``idx``.

    The graphs are shared with this dataset (not copied), and the
    ``transform`` of the dataset is still applied lazily when a graph is
    accessed.

    Args:
        idx: The graphs to select, as a slice, a list or array of indices
            (negative indices are allowed), or a boolean mask of shape
            ``[len(dataset)]``.

    Returns:
        The dataset restricted to the selected graphs.

    Example:

    .. code-block:: python

        subset = dataset.index_select([0, 2, 4])
        len(subset)
        # 3
    """
    indices = range(len(self))
    if isinstance(idx, slice):
        selected = list(indices[idx])
    else:
        idx_np = np.asarray(np.array(idx) if isinstance(idx, mx.array) else idx)
        idx_np = idx_np.reshape(-1)
        if idx_np.dtype == np.bool_:
            if idx_np.size != len(self):
                raise IndexError(
                    f"The boolean mask has {idx_np.size} entries but the "
                    f"dataset has {len(self)} graphs"
                )
            selected = np.nonzero(idx_np)[0].tolist()
        elif idx_np.size == 0 or np.issubdtype(idx_np.dtype, np.integer):
            selected = [indices[i] for i in idx_np.astype(np.int64).tolist()]
        else:
            raise IndexError(
                "Dataset indexing failed. Accepted indices are: slice, "
                "integer or boolean mx.array / np.ndarray, list, tuple "
                f"(got dtype '{idx_np.dtype}')"
            )

    dataset = copy.copy(self)
    dataset.graphs = [self.graphs[i] for i in selected]
    return dataset

def shuffle(
    self, return_perm: bool = False
) -> Union["Dataset", tuple["Dataset", mx.array]]:
    """Returns a copy of the dataset with the graphs in random order.

    The permutation comes from ``mx.random.permutation``, so it is
    reproducible with ``mx.random.seed``. The graphs themselves are shared,
    not copied.

    Args:
        return_perm: Whether to also return the permutation. Default:
            ``False``

    Returns:
        The shuffled dataset, and the permutation if ``return_perm`` is
        ``True`` (graph ``i`` of the shuffled dataset is graph ``perm[i]``
        of this one).

    Example:

    .. code-block:: python

        mx.random.seed(42)
        shuffled, perm = dataset.shuffle(return_perm=True)
    """
    perm = mx.random.permutation(len(self)).astype(mx.int32)
    dataset = self.index_select(perm)
    if return_perm:
        return dataset, perm
    return dataset

Bases: _KnowledgeGraphDataset

The FB15K237 dataset from the "Translating Embeddings for Modeling Multi-Relational Data" paper, containing 14,541 entities, 237 relations and 310,116 fact triples.

Each split is a separate graph whose edge_index holds the (head, tail) entity pairs and edge_type the relation of each triplet. Entity and relation ids are shared across the three splits, and each graph has num_nodes set to the total number of entities.

This dataset follows the implementation of PyG.

Note

The original FB15k dataset suffers from major test leakage through inverse relations, where a large number of test triples could be obtained by inverting triples in the training set. In order to create a dataset without this characteristic, FB15k_237 contains a subset of FB15k where inverse relations are removed.

def __init__(
    self,
    split: KG_SPLITS = "train",
    base_dir: Optional[str] = None,
    pre_transform: Optional[Callable] = None,
    transform: Optional[Callable] = None,

        pre_transform=pre_transform,

    self.graphs = [self.graphs[splits.index(split)]]

def __init__(
    self,
    num_graphs: int = 1,
    num_node_types: int = 3,
    num_edge_types: int = 6,
    avg_num_nodes: int = 1000,
    avg_degree: float = 10.0,
    avg_num_channels: int = 64,
    edge_dim: int = 0,
    num_classes: int = 10,
    task: FAKE_TASKS = "auto",
    seed: Optional[int] = None,
    pre_transform: Optional[Callable] = None,
    transform: Optional[Callable] = None,
    **kwargs: Union[int, tuple[int, ...]],
):
    if task == "auto":
        task = "graph" if num_graphs > 1 else "node"
    assert task in ["node", "graph"], "Invalid task"

    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    self._rng = rng
    self._num_graphs = max(num_graphs, 1)

    self.node_types = [f"v{i}" for i in range(max(num_node_types, 1))]
    pairs = list(product(self.node_types, self.node_types))
    edge_pairs: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
    while len(edge_pairs) < max(num_edge_types, 1):
        edge_pairs.extend(pairs)
    edge_pairs = [edge_pairs[i] for i in rng.permutation(len(edge_pairs))]
    self.edge_types: list[tuple[str, str, str]] = []
    count: dict[tuple[str, str], int] = defaultdict(int)
    for src, dst in edge_pairs[: max(num_edge_types, 1)]:
        self.edge_types.append((src, f"e{count[(src, dst)]}", dst))
        count[(src, dst)] += 1

    self.avg_num_nodes = max(avg_num_nodes, int(avg_degree))
    self.avg_degree = max(avg_degree, 1)
    self.num_channels = [
        _get_num_channels(rng, avg_num_channels) for _ in self.node_types
    ]
    self.edge_dim = edge_dim
    self._num_classes_ = num_classes
    self.task = task
    self.kwargs = kwargs
    super().__init__(
        name="fake_hetero", pre_transform=pre_transform, transform=transform
    )

Bases: Dataset

Datasets of the "Benchmarking Graph Neural Networks" paper.

  • "PATTERN" and "CLUSTER": node classification on graphs sampled from stochastic block models. In PATTERN, the task is to find the nodes of a planted pattern (2 classes); in CLUSTER, to find the cluster of each node, given a single labelled node per cluster (6 classes). Node features are given in node_features and labels in node_labels.
  • "CSL": graph classification of Circular Skip Link graphs into 10 isomorphism classes. The graphs have no features (only num_nodes) and the labels are in graph_labels. CSL has no standard split: only the "train" split exists and contains all the graphs (5-fold stratified cross-validation is recommended), as in PyG.

def __init__(
    self,
    name: str,
    split: GNN_BENCHMARK_SPLITS = "train",
    base_dir: Optional[str] = None,
    pre_transform: Optional[Callable] = None,
    transform: Optional[Callable] = None,
):
    if name in ("MNIST", "CIFAR10"):
        raise ValueError(f"Use mlx_graphs.datasets.SuperPixelDataset for '{name}'")
    if name in self.unsupported_names:
        raise ValueError(f"GNNBenchmarkDataset '{name}' is not available")
    if name not in self.names:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown dataset '{name}' (got {self.names})")
    if split not in _SPLIT_INDEX:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Split '{split}' found, but expected 'train', 'val' or 'test'"
        )
    if name == "CSL" and split != "train":
        warnings.warn(
            "Dataset 'CSL' does not provide a standardized splitting. "
            "Instead, it is recommended to perform 5-fold cross "
            "validation with stratifed sampling"
        )
        split = "train"
    self.split = split
    super().__init__(
        name=name,
        base_dir=base_dir,
        pre_transform=pre_transform,
        transform=transform,
    )

The Peptides datasets of the "Long Range Graph Benchmark" (LRGB).

Graphs are peptides (molecules made of chains of amino acids) and the tasks require long-range interactions. Node and edge features are the categorical atom and bond features of OGB (9 and 3 integer features per node and edge, to be embedded e.g. with one nn.Embedding per feature).

  • "peptides-func": multi-label graph classification of 10 peptide functions (graph_labels of shape [1, 10], float), evaluated with the average precision.
  • "peptides-struct": graph regression of 11 3D structural properties (graph_labels of shape [1, 11], float), evaluated with the mean absolute error.

This dataset follows the implementation of PyG and reads the same raw files, without requiring PyTorch. The graphs are the same, in the same order, with int32 indices and features. The superpixel datasets "pascalvoc-sp" and "coco-sp" (382 MB and 4.1 GB downloads) and "pcqm-contact" are not available.

Bases: PackedGraphsMixin, Dataset

The MoleculeNet benchmark collection from the "MoleculeNet: A Benchmark for Molecular Machine Learning" paper, containing datasets of physical chemistry, biophysics and physiology.

The molecules are given as SMILES strings and converted to graphs with from_smiles() (which requires rdkit): each graph has int32 node_features of shape [num_atoms, 9] and edge_features of shape [num_edges, 3] (categorical atom and bond features, see x_map and e_map), the SMILES string in smiles and the float32 targets in graph_labels, of shape [1, num_tasks], with NaN for missing labels (classification targets are 0.0 / 1.0).

This dataset follows the implementation of PyG and reads the same raw files, without requiring PyTorch. The graphs are the same, in the same order (with int32 instead of int64 indices and features). Molecules without atoms (e.g. SMILES strings that RDKit cannot parse) are skipped, with a warning, so the number of graphs depends slightly on the RDKit version (e.g. 2,039 graphs for BBBP, 7,823 for Tox21 and 41,120 for HIV with RDKit 2026.9, as in PyG).

Bases: Dataset

Datasets from the Open Graph Benchmark (OGB) collection of realistic, large-scale, and diverse benchmark datasets for machine learning on graphs.

Datasets belongs to three fundamental graph machine learning task categories: predicting the properties of nodes, links, and graphs. Node property prediction datasets consist of a single graph with three additional properties: train_mask, val_mask and test_mask specifying the masks for the train, validation and test splits. Link property prediction datasets also consist of a single graphs with three additional properties: train_edge_index, val_edge_index and test_edge_index, specifying the edges to be considered for training, validation and testing. Bases: HeteroDataset

The ogbn-mag dataset from the "Open Graph Benchmark: Datasets for Machine Learning on Graphs" paper, a heterogeneous subset of the Microsoft Academic Graph, as PyG's OGB_MAG.

It has four node types: papers (736,389), authors (1,134,649), institutions (8,740) and fields of study (59,965), and four edge types: author -affiliated_with-> institution, author -writes-> paper, paper -cites-> paper and paper -has_topic-> field_of_study (21.1M edges in total). The task is to predict the venue (349 classes) of each paper. Papers have 128-dimensional word2vec features and a publication year; the other node types have no features. The split is by year (train: until 2017, validation: 2018, test: 2019).

The graph is a HeteroGraphData with:

  • edge_index_dict: the four edge types (int32, no reverse edges; message passing models such as to_hetero() need reverse edge types so that every node type receives messages, see add_reverse_edges()),
  • node_features_dict["paper"] ([736389, 128]) and node_labels_dict["paper"] ([736389]),
  • num_nodes_dict with the number of nodes of every node type,
  • paper_year and the boolean masks paper_train_mask, paper_val_mask and paper_test_mask.

The raw data (a 430 MB download) is read with pandas. The processed graph is stored as safetensors and loaded lazily.

Adds a reverse edge type (dst, "rev_<rel>", src) for every edge type between two different node types, and makes paper -cites-> paper undirected (both directions, duplicates removed), like PyG's ToUndirected transform, so that every node type receives messages.

@staticmethod
def add_reverse_edges(data: HeteroGraphData) -> HeteroGraphData:
    """Adds a reverse edge type ``(dst, "rev_<rel>", src)`` for every edge
    type between two different node types, and makes ``paper -cites->
    paper`` undirected (both directions, duplicates removed), like PyG's
    ``ToUndirected`` transform, so that every node type receives messages.

    Args:
        data: The ogbn-mag graph.

    Returns:
        The same graph, with the new edge types.
    """
    edge_index_dict = dict(data.edge_index_dict)
    for (src, rel, dst), edge_index in data.edge_index_dict.items():
        if src == dst:
            both = np.concatenate(
                [np.array(edge_index), np.array(edge_index[::-1])], axis=1
            )
            both = np.unique(both, axis=1)
            edge_index_dict[(src, rel, dst)] = mx.array(both.astype(np.int32))
        else:
            edge_index_dict[(dst, f"rev_{rel}", src)] = edge_index[::-1]
    data.edge_index_dict = edge_index_dict
    return data

The protein-protein interaction networks from the "Predicting Multicellular Function through Multi-layer Tissue Networks" paper, containing positional gene sets, motif gene sets and immunological signatures as features (50 in total) and gene ontology sets as labels (121 in total), as used by GraphSAGE.

The dataset has 24 graphs (one per human tissue): 20 for training, 2 for validation and 2 for testing. The task is multi-label node classification: node_labels holds 121 binary (float32) targets per node. Edges are undirected (both directions are stored) and self-loops are removed, as in PyG.

PyG reads DGL's ppi.zip, which is the GraphSAGE release split into one file per split with a graph id per node. As DGL's server is no longer reachable, this dataset reads the GraphSAGE release directly: nodes, features, labels and edges are the same, and the graphs (stored one after the other) are recovered as the node ranges that no edge crosses (this gives exactly 20 / 2 / 2 graphs, with PyG's 44,906 / 6,514 / 5,524 nodes and 1,226,368 training edges). Edges are sorted by (source, target).

Bases: PackedGraphsMixin, Dataset

The QM9 dataset from the "MoleculeNet: A Benchmark for Molecular Machine Learning" paper, consisting of about 130,000 small organic molecules (up to 9 heavy atoms among C, O, N and F) with 19 regression targets.

Each molecule includes the 3D coordinates of the atoms of its low-energy conformation, and the atom features of the "Neural Message Passing for Quantum Chemistry" paper. Each graph has:

  • node_features: float32 [num_atoms, 11], the one-hot atom type (H, C, N, O, F), atomic number, aromaticity, sp / sp2 / sp3 hybridization and number of hydrogens;
  • z: int32 [num_atoms], the atomic numbers;
  • pos: float32 [num_atoms, 3], the coordinates (in Å);
  • edge_index and edge_features (float32 [num_edges, 4], the one-hot bond type: single, double, triple, aromatic);
  • graph_labels: float32 [1, 19], the targets below;
  • name (e.g. "gdb_1"), idx (index in the raw data) and, when processed with RDKit, smiles.
Target Property Description Unit 0 \(\mu\) Dipole moment D 1 \(\alpha\) Isotropic polarizability \({a_0}^3\) 2 \(\epsilon_{\textrm{HOMO}}\) Highest occupied molecular orbital energy eV 3 \(\epsilon_{\textrm{LUMO}}\) Lowest unoccupied molecular orbital energy eV 4 \(\Delta \epsilon\) Gap between HOMO and LUMO eV 5 \(\langle R^2 \rangle\) Electronic spatial extent \({a_0}^2\) 6 ZPVE Zero point vibrational energy eV 7 \(U_0\) Internal energy at 0K eV 8 \(U\) Internal energy at 298.15K eV 9 \(H\) Enthalpy at 298.15K eV 10 \(G\) Free energy at 298.15K eV 11 \(c_{\textrm{v}}\) Heat capacity at 298.15K cal/(mol K) 12 \(U_0^{\textrm{ATOM}}\) Atomization energy at 0K eV 13 \(U^{\textrm{ATOM}}\) Atomization energy at 298.15K eV 14 \(H^{\textrm{ATOM}}\) Atomization enthalpy at 298.15K eV 15 \(G^{\textrm{ATOM}}\) Atomization free energy at 298.15K eV 16 \(A\) Rotational constant GHz 17 \(B\) Rotational constant GHz 18 \(C\) Rotational constant GHz

This dataset follows the implementation of PyG: if rdkit is installed, the raw SDF files are processed (as PyG does with RDKit), otherwise PyG's pre-processed version of the dataset is read (without PyTorch). Both give the same graphs, except for the smiles attribute that is only available with RDKit.

def atomref(self, target: int) -> Optional[mx.array]:
    """The reference single-atom properties for the target ``target``
    (indexed by atomic number), of shape ``[100, 1]``, or ``None`` if the
    target has none (only targets 6 to 11 have one). Used as the
    ``atomref`` of :class:`~mlx_graphs.nn.SchNet`."""
    if target not in _ATOMREFS:
        return None
    out = np.zeros(100, dtype=np.float32)
    out[[1, 6, 7, 8, 9]] = _ATOMREFS[target]
    return mx.array(out.reshape(-1, 1))

def __init__(
    self,
    categories: Optional[Union[str, List[str]]] = None,
    include_normals: bool = True,
    split: SHAPENET_SPLITS = "trainval",
    base_dir: Optional[str] = None,
    pre_transform: Optional[Callable] = None,
    transform: Optional[Callable] = None,
):
    if categories is None:
        categories = list(self.category_ids)
    if isinstance(categories, str):
        categories = [categories]
    unknown = [c for c in categories if c not in self.category_ids]
    if unknown:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown categories {unknown}")
    if split not in ("train", "val", "test", "trainval"):
        raise ValueError(
            f"Split {split} found, but expected either train, val, trainval "
            "or test"
        )
    self.categories = list(categories)
    self.include_normals = include_normals
    self.split = split
    super().__init__(
        name="ShapeNet",
        base_dir=base_dir,
        pre_transform=pre_transform,
        transform=transform,
    )
    if not include_normals:
        for graph in self.graphs:
            graph.node_features = None
    mask = np.zeros((len(self.seg_classes), 50), dtype=bool)
    for i, labels in enumerate(self.seg_classes.values()):
        mask[i, labels] = True
    self.y_mask = mx.array(mask)

Bases: _TGBDataset

The dynamic link property prediction datasets of the Temporal Graph Benchmark (TGB), as py-tgb's tgb.linkproppred.dataset_pyg.PyGLinkPropPredDataset.

The dataset is a single TemporalData stream of events sorted by time, with src and dst the nodes, t the timestamps (int64), msg the edge features, w the edge weights and y all ones (the label of a true edge). The events are split chronologically at the 70% and 85% quantiles of the timestamps (train_mask, val_mask, test_mask) and every validation and test event comes with a fixed set of negative destinations (see TGBNegativeEdgeSampler; 999 per event for "tgbl-wiki", 100 for "tgbl-review"), against which it is ranked to compute the mean reciprocal rank (MRR) with the TGBEvaluator.

================= ========== =========== ========== Name #nodes #events #features ================= ========== =========== ========== "tgbl-wiki" 9,227 157,474 172 "tgbl-review" 352,637 4,873,540 1 "tgbl-coin" 638,486 22,809,486 1 "tgbl-comment" 994,790 44,314,507 3 "tgbl-flight" 18,143 67,169,570 16 ================= ========== =========== ==========

The node ids and features are those of py-tgb (the processing of each raw file is the same): "tgbl-wiki" numbers the items after the users and its features are the JODIE Wikipedia features; "tgbl-review" and "tgbl-coin" number the nodes in order of first appearance and their feature is log2 of the edge weight (w, zero weights count as 1); "tgbl-comment" has the number of words (divided by 5,000, twice) and the score of the comments; "tgbl-flight" encodes the call sign and aircraft type code as characters, and has node features (node_feat, the type, continent, region and coordinates of the airports).

def load_eval_set(self, fname: str, split_mode: str = "val"):
    """Loads the negative samples of a split.

    Args:
        fname: A ``.npz`` file written by :func:`convert_tgb_negatives`
            (or a TGB ``.pkl`` file, which is then converted next to it)
        split_mode: ``"val"`` or ``"test"``
    """
    if split_mode not in _SPLITS:
        raise ValueError("Invalid split-mode! It should be `val` or `test`")
    if not os.path.exists(fname):
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"File not found at {fname}")
    if fname.endswith(".pkl"):
        npz = fname[: -len(".pkl")] + ".npz"
        if not os.path.exists(npz):
            convert_tgb_negatives(fname, npz)
        fname = npz
    with np.load(fname, allow_pickle=False) as f:
        keys, neg, num_neg = f["keys"], f["neg"], f["num_neg"]
    keys = _make_keys([keys[:, i] for i in range(keys.shape[1])])
    order = np.argsort(keys, kind="stable")
    self.eval_set[split_mode] = {
        "keys": keys[order],
        "neg": neg[order],
        "num_neg": num_neg[order],
    }

def query_batch(
    self,
    pos_src: Any,
    pos_dst: Any,
    pos_timestamp: Any,
    edge_type: Any = None,
    split_mode: str = "test",
) -> list[list[int]]:
    """Negative destinations of each positive edge, as ``py-tgb``.

    Args:
        pos_src: Sources of the positive edges, shape `[batch_size]`
        pos_dst: Destinations of the positive edges
        pos_timestamp: Timestamps of the positive edges
        edge_type: Edge types (only for datasets with typed edges)
        split_mode: ``"val"`` or ``"test"``

    Returns:
        A list with the list of negative destinations of every positive
        edge.
    """
    eval_set, rows = self._rows(
        pos_src, pos_dst, pos_timestamp, edge_type, split_mode
    )
    neg, num_neg = eval_set["neg"][rows], eval_set["num_neg"][rows]
    return [row[:n].tolist() for row, n in zip(neg, num_neg)]

def query_batch_array(
    self,
    pos_src: Any,
    pos_dst: Any,
    pos_timestamp: Any,
    edge_type: Any = None,
    split_mode: str = "test",
) -> tuple[mx.array, mx.array]:
    """Negative destinations of each positive edge as a padded array.

    Most positive edges of a split have the same number of negatives, a
    few have less: their rows are padded with ``-1``. Give the scores of
    the padding entries the value ``-inf`` before passing them to the
    :class:`~mlx_graphs.metrics.TGBEvaluator`, so that they never rank
    above the positive.

    Args:
        pos_src: Sources of the positive edges, shape `[batch_size]`
        pos_dst: Destinations of the positive edges
        pos_timestamp: Timestamps of the positive edges
        edge_type: Edge types (only for datasets with typed edges)
        split_mode: ``"val"`` or ``"test"``

    Returns:
        The negative destinations, shape `[batch_size, max_num_neg]`, and
        the boolean mask of the valid (non-padding) entries.
    """
    eval_set, rows = self._rows(
        pos_src, pos_dst, pos_timestamp, edge_type, split_mode
    )
    num_neg = eval_set["num_neg"][rows]
    width = int(num_neg.max()) if num_neg.size else 0
    neg = eval_set["neg"][rows, :width]
    mask = np.arange(width)[None, :] < num_neg[:, None]
    return mx.array(neg), mx.array(mask)

Bases: _TGBDataset

The dynamic node property prediction datasets of the Temporal Graph Benchmark (TGB), as py-tgb's tgb.nodeproppred.dataset_pyg.PyGNodePropPredDataset.

The dataset is a single TemporalData stream of weighted events sorted by time (msg holds the weights), split chronologically (train_mask, val_mask, test_mask). The task is to predict, at given timestamps, the distribution of the future interactions of some nodes over num_classes items (e.g. the share of each trading partner of a nation the next year, or of each music genre of a user the next week), evaluated with NDCG@10 (TGBEvaluator).

The labels form a stream of label timestamps (label_timestamps). As in py-tgb, get_node_label() returns the labels of the next label timestamp once the events reach it, and reset_label_time() rewinds the stream at the start of every pass over the events. node_labels() gives the labels of any label timestamp directly.

================= ========== =========== ========= ========== Name #nodes #events #classes #features ================= ========== =========== ========= ========== "tgbn-trade" 255 468,245 255 1 "tgbn-genre" 1,505 17,858,395 513 1 "tgbn-reddit" 11,766 27,174,118 698 1 "tgbn-token" 61,756 72,936,998 1,001 2 ================= ========== =========== ========= ==========

The node ids are those of py-tgb: the classes (genres, subreddits, tokens) are the nodes 0 to num_classes - 1 and the users are numbered after them; the nations of "tgbn-trade" are both the nodes and the classes. The features are the edge weights (and, for "tgbn-token", whether the user is the sender), with the natural logarithm of the weights for "tgbn-token" (as py-tgb once its processed files are cached).

def node_labels(self, i: int) -> tuple[mx.array, mx.array, mx.array]:
    """The node labels of the ``i``-th label timestamp.

    Args:
        i: Index in :attr:`label_timestamps`

    Returns:
        The timestamp repeated for every labeled node, the labeled nodes,
        and their label vectors (float32, shape `[num_nodes, label_dim]`),
        in the order of ``py-tgb``.
    """
    a = self.arrays
    start, end = int(a["label_ptr"][i]), int(a["label_ptr"][i + 1])
    nodes = a["label_node"][start:end]
    labels = np.zeros((end - start, self.label_dim), dtype=np.float32)
    e_start, e_end = a["label_entry_ptr"][start], a["label_entry_ptr"][end]
    rows = np.repeat(
        np.arange(end - start), np.diff(a["label_entry_ptr"][start : end + 1])
    )
    labels[rows, a["label_class"][e_start:e_end]] = a["label_value"][e_start:e_end]
    ts = np.full(end - start, a["label_ts"][i], dtype=np.int64)
    return mx.array(ts), mx.array(nodes.astype(np.int32)), mx.array(labels)

def get_node_label(
    self, cur_t: Union[int, mx.array]
) -> Optional[tuple[mx.array, mx.array, mx.array]]:
    """The labels of the next label timestamp if ``cur_t`` reached it, as
    ``py-tgb``'s ``get_node_label``: the label stream then moves to the
    following label timestamp. Returns ``None`` otherwise (or after the
    last label timestamp).

    Args:
        cur_t: The current time (e.g. the time of the last event of a
            mini-batch)

    Returns:
        ``(label_ts, label_nodes, labels)``, see :meth:`node_labels`.
    """
    if isinstance(cur_t, mx.array):
        cur_t = cur_t.item()
    if self.label_ts_idx >= self.num_label_timestamps:
        return None
    if cur_t >= self.arrays["label_ts"][self.label_ts_idx]:
        self.label_ts_idx += 1
        return self.node_labels(self.label_ts_idx - 1)
    return None

def get_label_time(self) -> int:
    """The next label timestamp of the stream (the last one once the

The WebKB datasets used in the "Geom-GCN: Geometric Graph Convolutional Networks" paper.

Nodes represent web pages and edges represent hyperlinks between them. Node features are the bag-of-words representation of web pages. The task is to classify the nodes into one of the five categories: student, project, course, staff, and faculty. The graphs are directed and strongly heterophilous.

The 10 fixed train/validation/test splits (60%/20%/20%) of the Geom-GCN paper are stored as masks of shape [num_nodes, 10] in the train_mask, val_mask and test_mask attributes.

This dataset follows the implementation of PyG.

The ZINC dataset from the ZINC database and the "Automatic Chemical Design Using a Data-Driven Continuous Representation of Molecules" paper, containing about 250,000 molecular graphs with up to 38 heavy atoms.

The task is to regress the penalized logP (also called constrained solubility), given by y = logP - SAS - cycles, where logP is the water-octanol partition coefficient, SAS the synthetic accessibility score and cycles the number of cycles with more than six atoms.

Each graph has int32 node_features of shape [num_atoms, 1] (the atom type, 28 types), int32 edge_features of shape [num_edges] (the bond type: 1 single, 2 double, 3 triple) and a float32 graph_labels of shape [1].

This dataset follows the implementation of PyG and reads the same raw files, without requiring PyTorch. The graphs are the same, in the same order (with int32 instead of int64 indices and features).

def check_sha1(filename: str, sha1_hash: str) -> bool:
    """Check whether the sha1 hash of the file content matches the expected hash.

    Code borrowed from dgl

    Args:
        filename: Path to the file.
        sha1_hash: Expected sha1 hash in hexadecimal digits.

    Returns:
        Whether the file content matches the expected hash.
    """
    # SHA1 used for download integrity check, not security
    sha1 = hashlib.sha1(usedforsecurity=False)
    with open(filename, "rb") as f:
        while True:
            data = f.read(1048576)
            if not data:
                break
            sha1.update(data)

    return sha1.hexdigest() == sha1_hash

def download(
    url: str,
    path: Optional[str] = None,
    overwrite: bool = True,
    sha1_hash: Optional[str] = None,
    retries: int = 5,
    verify_ssl: bool = True,
    log: bool = True,
) -> str:
    """Download a given URL.

    Code borrowed from dgl

    Args:
        url: URL to download.
        path: Destination path to store downloaded file. By default stores to the
            current directory with the same name as in url.
        overwrite: Whether to overwrite the destination file if it already exists.
            By default always overwrites the downloaded file.
        sha1_hash: Expected sha1 hash in hexadecimal digits. Will ignore existing file
            when hash is specified but doesn't match.
        retries: The number of times to attempt downloading in case of failure or non
            200 return codes.
        verify_ssl: Verify SSL certificates.
        log: Whether to print the progress for download

    Returns:
        The file path of the downloaded file.
    """
    if path is None:
        fname = url.split("/")[-1]
        # Empty filenames are invalid
        assert fname, (
            "Can't construct file-name from this URL. "
            "Please set the `path` option manually."
        )
    else:
        path = os.path.expanduser(path)
        if os.path.isdir(path):
            fname = os.path.join(path, url.split("/")[-1])
        else:
            fname = path
    assert retries >= 0, "Number of retries should be at least 0"

    if not verify_ssl:
        warnings.warn(
            "Unverified HTTPS request is being made (verify_ssl=False). "
            "Adding certificate verification is strongly advised."
        )

    if (
        overwrite
        or not os.path.exists(fname)
        or (sha1_hash and not check_sha1(fname, sha1_hash))
    ):
        dirname = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(os.path.expanduser(fname)))
        if not os.path.exists(dirname):
            os.makedirs(dirname)
        while retries + 1 > 0:
            # Disable pyling too broad Exception
            # pylint: disable=W0703
            try:
                if log:
                    print("Downloading %s from %s..." % (fname, url))
                r = requests.get(  # nosec B113 - timeout tuple covers connect + read
                    url, stream=True, verify=verify_ssl, timeout=(30, 300)
                )
                if r.status_code != 200:
                    raise RuntimeError("Failed downloading url %s" % url)
                # Sizes in bytes.
                total_size = int(r.headers.get("content-length", 0))
                block_size = 1024

                with tqdm(total=total_size, unit="B", unit_scale=True) as progress_bar:
                    with open(fname, "wb") as f:
                        for chunk in r.iter_content(chunk_size=block_size):
                            progress_bar.update(len(chunk))
                            if chunk:  # filter out keep-alive new chunks
                                f.write(chunk)
                if sha1_hash and not check_sha1(fname, sha1_hash):
                    raise UserWarning(
                        "File {} is downloaded but the content hash does not match."
                        " The repo may be outdated or download may be incomplete. "
                        'If the "repo_url" is overridden, consider switching to '
                        "the default repo.".format(fname)
                    )
                break
            except Exception as e:
                retries -= 1
                if retries <= 0:
                    raise e
                else:
                    if log:
                        print(
                            "download failed, retrying, {} attempt{} left".format(
                                retries, "s" if retries > 1 else ""
                            )
                        )

    return fname

def extract_archive(file: str, target_dir: str, overwrite=True):
    """Extract archive file.

    Code borrowed from dgl

    Args:
        file: Absolute path of the archive file.
        target_dir: Target directory of the archive to be uncompressed.
        overwrite: Whether to overwrite the contents inside the directory.
            By default always overwrites.
    """
    if os.path.exists(target_dir) and not overwrite:
        return
    print("Extracting file to {}".format(target_dir))
    if file.endswith(".tar.gz") or file.endswith(".tar") or file.endswith(".tgz"):
        import tarfile

        with tarfile.open(file, "r") as archive:
            abs_target = os.path.abspath(target_dir)

            def is_within_target(path: str) -> bool:
                # `commonpath` compares whole path components: unlike a
                # string prefix, "<target>_evil" is not inside "<target>".
                path = os.path.abspath(path)
                return os.path.commonpath([abs_target, path]) == abs_target

            for member in archive.getmembers():
                member_path = os.path.join(abs_target, member.name)
                if not is_within_target(member_path):
                    raise Exception("Attempted Path Traversal in Tar File")
                # Links must not point outside either: files extracted later
                # could be written through them.
                if member.issym() or member.islnk():
                    base = (
                        os.path.dirname(member_path) if member.issym() else abs_target
                    )
                    if not is_within_target(os.path.join(base, member.linkname)):
                        raise Exception("Attempted Path Traversal in Tar File")
            if hasattr(tarfile, "data_filter"):  # Python >= 3.12 and backports
                archive.extractall(target_dir, filter="data")  # nosec B202
            else:  # members validated above
                archive.extractall(target_dir)  # nosec B202
    elif file.endswith(".gz"):
        import gzip
        import shutil

        with gzip.open(file, "rb") as f_in:
            target_file = os.path.join(target_dir, os.path.basename(file)[:-3])
            with open(target_file, "wb") as f_out:
                shutil.copyfileobj(f_in, f_out)
    elif file.endswith(".zip"):
        import zipfile

        with zipfile.ZipFile(file, "r") as archive:
            abs_target = os.path.abspath(target_dir)
            for name in archive.namelist():
                member_path = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(target_dir, name))
                if os.path.commonpath([abs_target, member_path]) != abs_target:
                    raise Exception("Attempted Path Traversal in Zip File")
            archive.extractall(path=target_dir)  # nosec B202 - members validated above
    else:
        raise Exception("Unrecognized file type: " + file)

def load_torch_file(path: Union[str, os.PathLike]) -> Any:
    """Loads a file saved with ``torch.save`` (or a plain pickle file) without
    PyTorch, with every tensor converted to a :class:`numpy.ndarray`.

    Both the zip-based format (default since PyTorch 1.6) and the legacy
    format are supported. Only tensors (on any device, read on the CPU),
    containers (lists, tuples, dicts), NumPy arrays and SciPy COO matrices
    (read as :class:`SparseCOOMatrix`) can be loaded: any other object raises
    a :class:`pickle.UnpicklingError`, which makes the loader safe to use on
    untrusted files. ``bfloat16`` and complex tensors are not supported.

    Args:
        path: Path of the file.

    Returns:
        The saved object, with tensors as NumPy arrays.

    Example:

    .. code-block:: python

        from mlx_graphs.datasets.utils import load_torch_file

        graphs = load_torch_file("peptidesfunc/train.pt")
        node_features, edge_features, edge_index, y = graphs[0]
    """
    path = os.fspath(path)
    if zipfile.is_zipfile(path):
        return _load_zip(path)
    with open(path, "rb") as f:
        first = f.read(64)
        f.seek(0)
        # A legacy torch file starts with the pickled magic number, which is a
        # LONG1 opcode (``\x8a``) right after the protocol header.
        if len(first) > 2 and first[0] == 0x80 and first[2] == 0x8A:
            return _load_legacy(f)
        return _materialize(_RestrictedUnpickler(f, {}).load())

def parse_txt_array(
    src: list[str],
    sep: str,
    dtype: mx.Dtype,
    start: int = 0,
    end: Optional[int] = None,
) -> mx.array:
    to_number = float if is_floating_point(dtype) else int
    parsed_src = [[to_number(x) for x in line.split(sep)[start:end]] for line in src]
    parsed_array = mx.array(parsed_src, dtype=dtype).squeeze()
    return parsed_array

Partitions a graph into num_parts clusters, for Cluster-GCN training ("Cluster-GCN: An Efficient Algorithm for Training Deep and Large Graph Convolutional Networks"), following PyG's ClusterData. Use it with ClusterLoader.

PyG partitions with METIS. Here, METIS (through the optional pymetis package) is used only if it is installed or method="metis" is set; otherwise a dependency-free balanced partitioner is used (see balanced_partition()): partitions are balanced but differ from METIS', with a usually larger edge cut. Any custom partition can also be given with partition.

cluster_data[i] is the subgraph induced by the nodes of cluster i (edges between clusters are dropped), with n_id and e_id.

def __init__(
    self,
    data: GraphData,
    num_parts: int,
    partition: Optional[Union[mx.array, np.ndarray]] = None,
    method: Literal["auto", "metis", "balanced"] = "auto",
    num_iters: int = 10,
):
    if method not in ("auto", "metis", "balanced"):
        raise ValueError(
            f"`method` must be 'auto', 'metis' or 'balanced' (got '{method}')"
        )
    self.data = data
    self.num_nodes = data.num_nodes
    self.num_edges = data.num_edges

    if partition is not None:
        cluster = to_numpy(partition).reshape(-1).astype(np.int64)
        if cluster.size != self.num_nodes:
            raise ValueError(
                f"`partition` has {cluster.size} entries, expected "
                f"{self.num_nodes} (one per node)."
            )
        if cluster.size and cluster.min() < 0:
            raise ValueError("`partition` must contain non-negative ids.")
        num_parts = int(cluster.max()) + 1 if cluster.size else 0
        self.method = "custom"
    else:
        has_metis = importlib.util.find_spec("pymetis") is not None
        if method == "metis" or (method == "auto" and has_metis):
            cluster = _metis_partition(data.edge_index, self.num_nodes, num_parts)
            self.method = "metis"
        else:
            cluster = balanced_partition(
                data.edge_index, self.num_nodes, num_parts, num_iters=num_iters
            )
            self.method = "balanced"

    self.num_parts = num_parts
    self.cluster = cluster
    self.node_perm = np.argsort(cluster, kind="stable")
    self.partptr = np.zeros(num_parts + 1, dtype=np.int64)
    np.cumsum(np.bincount(cluster, minlength=num_parts), out=self.partptr[1:])
    self._adj = Adjacency(data.edge_index, self.num_nodes)

def nodes_of(self, parts: Union[int, np.ndarray, list]) -> np.ndarray:
    """Global ids of the nodes of the given cluster(s), cluster by cluster."""
    parts = np.atleast_1d(np.asarray(parts, dtype=np.int64))
    starts = self.partptr[parts]
    return self.node_perm[segment_arange(starts, self.partptr[parts + 1] - starts)]

def subgraph(self, parts: Union[int, np.ndarray, list]) -> GraphData:
    """Subgraph induced by the union of the given clusters."""
    n_id = self.nodes_of(parts)
    edge_index, e_id = self._adj.induced_subgraph(n_id)
    return slice_graph(
        self.data,
        n_id,
        e_id,
        edge_index,
        num_nodes=self.num_nodes,
        num_edges=self.num_edges,
        n_id=index_array(n_id, self.num_nodes),
        e_id=index_array(e_id, self.num_edges),
    )

def __init__(
    self,
    dataset: Union[Dataset, Sequence[GraphData]],
    batch_size: int = 1,
    shuffle: bool = False,
    drop_last: bool = False,
    follow_batch: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None,
    sampler: Optional[Iterable[int]] = None,
    batch_sampler: Optional[Iterable[Sequence[int]]] = None,
    transform: Optional[Callable[[GraphData], GraphData]] = None,
    collate_fn: Optional[Callable[[list[GraphData]], Any]] = None,
):
    if batch_size < 1:
        raise ValueError(f"`batch_size` must be positive (got {batch_size}).")
    if sampler is not None and shuffle:
        raise ValueError("`sampler` and `shuffle` are mutually exclusive.")
    if batch_sampler is not None and (
        batch_size != 1 or shuffle or sampler is not None or drop_last
    ):
        raise ValueError(
            "`batch_sampler` is mutually exclusive with `batch_size`, "
            "`shuffle`, `sampler` and `drop_last`."
        )
    if follow_batch and collate_fn is not None:
        raise ValueError("`follow_batch` requires the default `collate_fn`.")

    self.dataset = dataset
    self.batch_size = batch_size
    self.shuffle = shuffle
    self.drop_last = drop_last
    self.follow_batch = list(follow_batch or [])
    self.sampler = sampler
    self.batch_sampler = batch_sampler
    self.transform = transform
    self.collate_fn = collate_fn

    self._indices = list(range(len(dataset)))
    self._batches: Optional[list[list[int]]] = None
    self._current_index = 0

Bases: GraphSAINTSampler

GraphSAINT edge sampler: samples batch_size edges without replacement with probability proportional to 1 / out_degree(source) + 1 / in_degree(target), and takes the subgraph induced by their endpoints.

Note

This follows the edge probabilities of the GraphSAINT paper (and of its reference implementation), which minimize the variance of the normalized aggregation. PyG's implementation instead uses in_degree(source) + out_degree(target), which favors the edges between high-degree nodes, and draws the batch_size edges with replacement.

See GraphSAINTSampler for the arguments and the batch content.

Example:

from mlx_graphs.loaders import GraphSAINTEdgeSampler

loader = GraphSAINTEdgeSampler(data, batch_size=4000, num_steps=5)

def __init__(
    self,
    data: GraphData,
    batch_size: int,
    num_steps: int = 1,
    sample_coverage: int = 0,
    save_dir: Optional[str] = None,
):
    if batch_size < 1:
        raise ValueError(f"`batch_size` must be positive (got {batch_size})")
    for name in ("node_norm", "edge_norm"):
        if getattr(data, name, None) is not None:
            raise ValueError(f"`data` already has a '{name}' attribute.")

    self.data = data
    self.batch_size = batch_size
    self.num_steps = num_steps
    self.sample_coverage = sample_coverage
    self.save_dir = save_dir

    self.N = data.num_nodes
    self.E = data.num_edges
    self._adj = Adjacency(data.edge_index, self.N)
    self._step = 0

    self.node_norm: Optional[np.ndarray] = None
    self.edge_norm: Optional[np.ndarray] = None
    if sample_coverage > 0:
        path = (
            os.path.join(save_dir, self._filename) if save_dir is not None else None
        )
        if path is not None and os.path.exists(path):
            saved = np.load(path)
            self.node_norm, self.edge_norm = saved["node_norm"], saved["edge_norm"]
        else:
            self.node_norm, self.edge_norm = self._compute_norm()
            if path is not None:
                os.makedirs(save_dir, exist_ok=True)  # type: ignore
                np.savez(path, node_norm=self.node_norm, edge_norm=self.edge_norm)

    batch_size: int,
    num_steps: int = 1,
    sample_coverage: int = 0,
    save_dir: Optional[str] = None,

Base class of the GraphSAINT samplers, from the "GraphSAINT: Graph Sampling Based Inductive Learning Method" paper, following PyG's GraphSAINTSampler.

Each iteration samples a set of nodes (how depends on the subclass) and yields the subgraph they induce, as a GraphData with node- and edge-level attributes sliced to the subgraph, plus n_id (global id of every node, sorted) and e_id (original id of every edge).

If sample_coverage > 0, normalization statistics are estimated beforehand by sampling subgraphs until every node has been sampled sample_coverage times on average, and every batch also holds:

  • node_norm: per-node loss weight, num_samples / (count(v) * N), to use as (node_norm * loss).sum();
  • edge_norm: per-edge aggregation weight, count(target(e)) / count(e), to scale messages with (with the default source -> target message passing, so that, for a sampled node, the expected normalized sum of the messages it receives equals the full-graph sum).
Note

PyG divides the count of the edge's source node instead (count(source(e)) / count(e)), which is the paper's normalization for the reverse edge: aggregations are then biased by count(source) / count(target) (several-fold for nodes of very different degrees). This class follows the paper, \(\alpha_{u,v} = p_{u,v} / p_v\) with \(v\) the aggregating node.

def __init__(
    self,
    data: GraphData,
    batch_size: int,
    num_steps: int = 1,
    sample_coverage: int = 0,
    save_dir: Optional[str] = None,
):
    if batch_size < 1:
        raise ValueError(f"`batch_size` must be positive (got {batch_size})")
    for name in ("node_norm", "edge_norm"):
        if getattr(data, name, None) is not None:
            raise ValueError(f"`data` already has a '{name}' attribute.")

    self.data = data
    self.batch_size = batch_size
    self.num_steps = num_steps
    self.sample_coverage = sample_coverage
    self.save_dir = save_dir

    self.N = data.num_nodes
    self.E = data.num_edges
    self._adj = Adjacency(data.edge_index, self.N)
    self._step = 0

    self.node_norm: Optional[np.ndarray] = None
    self.edge_norm: Optional[np.ndarray] = None
    if sample_coverage > 0:
        path = (
            os.path.join(save_dir, self._filename) if save_dir is not None else None
        )
        if path is not None and os.path.exists(path):
            saved = np.load(path)
            self.node_norm, self.edge_norm = saved["node_norm"], saved["edge_norm"]
        else:
            self.node_norm, self.edge_norm = self._compute_norm()
            if path is not None:
                os.makedirs(save_dir, exist_ok=True)  # type: ignore
                np.savez(path, node_norm=self.node_norm, edge_norm=self.edge_norm)

Bases: _HeteroNeighborLoader

Heterogeneous mini-batch loader using the layer-wise sampling of "Heterogeneous Graph Transformer" (HGSampling), as PyG's HGTLoader.

Instead of a number of neighbors per node (NeighborLoader), each hop samples a node budget per node type: every node type keeps a budget of candidate nodes, adjacent to the nodes sampled so far. Each sampled node adds 1 / degree to the budget of each of its (not yet sampled) neighbors, for every edge type pointing to it (nodes with more than 50 neighbors only add 1 / 50 to 50 random ones). At hop l, num_samples[node_type][l] nodes of each type are drawn from its budget without replacement, with probability proportional to the squared budget, which favours nodes connected to many sampled nodes. The mini-batch is the subgraph induced by the sampled nodes (for destination nodes with more than 50 neighbors, edges to 50 random ones, as in PyG).

Sampling runs on the host with NumPy (seed it with np.random.seed).

The first batch_size nodes of the seed node type are the seed nodes, so the loss is computed on them:

for batch in loader:
    out = model(batch.edge_index_dict, batch.node_features_dict)
    n = batch.batch_size
    loss = loss_fn(out["paper"][:n], batch.node_labels_dict["paper"][:n])

Each batch is a HeteroGraphData with the same attributes as the batches of NeighborLoader: edge_index_dict (local ids per node type), node_features_dict, node_labels_dict, edge_features_dict, n_id_dict (global id of every sampled node), e_id_dict (original position of every sampled edge), batch_size, input_type, num_nodes_dict, num_sampled_nodes_dict (number of nodes added at each hop, starting with the seeds), and the per-node attributes of data (e.g. paper_train_mask) sliced to the sampled nodes. Every node type and edge type is present, possibly empty.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default data HeteroGraphData

The full graph.

required num_samples Union[list[int], dict[str, list[int]]]

Number of nodes to sample per hop, either one list for every node type (e.g. [512] * 4) or a dict mapping each node type to its own list. Node types missing from the dict, or with a shorter list, sample no nodes at the missing hops.

required input_nodes Union[str, tuple[str, Optional[array]]]

The seed node type and which of its nodes to iterate over: "paper" (all papers), ("paper", indices) or ("paper", boolean_mask).

required batch_size int

Number of seed nodes per mini-batch.

1 shuffle bool

Whether to shuffle the seed nodes at the start of each epoch.

False sampler Optional[Iterable[int]]

Iterable yielding positions in input_nodes for each epoch (e.g. an ImbalancedSampler). Overrides shuffle. Duplicate seeds within a mini-batch are merged, so batch_size is then the number of distinct seeds.

None

Example:

from mlx_graphs.datasets import DBLP
from mlx_graphs.loaders import HGTLoader

data = DBLP()[0]
loader = HGTLoader(
    data,
    num_samples={
        "author": [512] * 2,
        "paper": [512] * 2,
        "term": [256] * 2,
        "conference": [20] * 2,
    },
    input_nodes=("author", data.author_train_mask),
    batch_size=128,
    shuffle=True,
)
batch = next(iter(loader))

def __init__(
    self,
    data: HeteroGraphData,
    num_samples: Union[list[int], dict[str, list[int]]],
    input_nodes: Union[str, tuple[str, Optional[mx.array]]],
    batch_size: int = 1,
    shuffle: bool = False,
    sampler: Optional[Iterable[int]] = None,
):
    if not isinstance(data, HeteroGraphData):
        raise TypeError(
            f"HGTLoader needs a HeteroGraphData, got {type(data).__name__}"
        )
    if isinstance(input_nodes, mx.array) or input_nodes is None:
        raise ValueError(
            "`input_nodes` must name the seed node type: 'paper', "
            "('paper', indices) or ('paper', boolean_mask)."
        )
    super().__init__(
        data,
        num_neighbors=[],
        input_nodes=input_nodes,
        batch_size=batch_size,
        shuffle=shuffle,
        sampler=sampler,
    )
    node_types = list(self.num_nodes)
    if isinstance(num_samples, dict):
        unknown = [t for t in num_samples if t not in self.num_nodes]
        if unknown:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown node types in num_samples: {unknown}")
        num_samples = {t: list(num_samples.get(t, [])) for t in node_types}
    else:
        num_samples = {t: list(num_samples) for t in node_types}
    if any(n < 0 for v in num_samples.values() for n in v):
        raise ValueError("num_samples must be non-negative")
    self.num_samples = num_samples
    self.num_hops = max((len(v) for v in num_samples.values()), default=0)

    self._colptr = {et: np.asarray(v) for et, v in self._colptr_dict.items()}
    self._row = {et: np.asarray(v) for et, v in self._row_dict.items()}
    self._perm = {et: np.asarray(v) for et, v in self._perm_dict.items()}
    self._edge_types = list(data.edge_index_dict)

def sample(self, seed_nodes: np.ndarray) -> tuple[dict, dict, dict, dict]:
    """Samples the subgraph of a mini-batch.

    Args:
        seed_nodes: Global ids of the (distinct) seed nodes of
            ``self.input_type``.

    Returns:
        ``(n_id_dict, edge_index_dict, e_id_dict, num_sampled_nodes_dict)``
        as NumPy arrays: the sampled nodes per node type (seeds first),
        the induced edges in local ids, their original edge positions, and
        the number of nodes added per hop.
    """
    node_types = list(self.num_nodes)
    nodes = {t: [] for t in node_types}
    counts = {t: [0] for t in node_types}
    local = {t: np.full(self.num_nodes[t], -1, dtype=np.int64) for t in node_types}
    budget = {t: np.zeros(self.num_nodes[t]) for t in node_types}

    def add(node_type, new):
        local[node_type][new] = sum(len(n) for n in nodes[node_type]) + np.arange(
            new.size
        )
        nodes[node_type].append(new)
        budget[node_type][new] = 0.0

    add(self.input_type, seed_nodes)
    counts[self.input_type][0] = seed_nodes.size
    self._update_budget(budget, local, self.input_type, seed_nodes)

    for hop in range(self.num_hops):
        samples = {}
        for node_type in node_types:
            plan = self.num_samples[node_type]
            k = plan[hop] if hop < len(plan) else 0
            candidates = np.nonzero(budget[node_type] > 0)[0]
            samples[node_type] = _weighted_sample(
                candidates, budget[node_type][candidates] ** 2, k
            )
            add(node_type, samples[node_type])
            counts[node_type].append(samples[node_type].size)
        if hop < self.num_hops - 1:
            for node_type, new in samples.items():
                self._update_budget(budget, local, node_type, new)

    n_id = {
        t: np.concatenate(v) if v else np.zeros(0, dtype=np.int64)
        for t, v in nodes.items()
    }

    # Induced subgraph (at most 50 random in-neighbors per destination).
    edge_index, e_id = {}, {}
    for edge_type in self._edge_types:
        src, _, dst = edge_type
        owner, pos, _ = _capped_neighbors(self._colptr[edge_type], n_id[dst])
        src_local = local[src][self._row[edge_type][pos]]
        keep = src_local >= 0
        edge_index[edge_type] = np.stack([src_local[keep], owner[keep]])
        e_id[edge_type] = self._perm[edge_type][pos[keep]]
    return n_id, edge_index, e_id, counts

Samples elements with probabilities inversely proportional to the frequency of their class, to rebalance an imbalanced classification task.

Indices are drawn with replacement. The sampler can be passed as sampler to:

  • Dataloader, for graph classification (dataset is a Dataset or a list of GraphData with one graph_labels entry each);
  • NeighborLoader, for node classification (dataset is the GraphData, and input_nodes the same seed nodes as given to the loader). It then yields positions in input_nodes.
