def __init__(
    self,
    dataset: Union[GraphData, Dataset, Sequence[GraphData], mx.array, np.ndarray],
    input_nodes: Optional[Union[mx.array, np.ndarray]] = None,
    num_samples: Optional[int] = None,
):
    if isinstance(dataset, GraphData):
        if dataset.node_labels is None:
            raise ValueError("The graph has no `node_labels`.")
        y = to_numpy(dataset.node_labels).reshape(-1)
        if y.size != dataset.num_nodes:
            raise ValueError("ImbalancedSampler requires one label per node.")
        y = y[to_index(input_nodes, y.size)]
    elif isinstance(dataset, (mx.array, np.ndarray)):
        y = to_numpy(dataset).reshape(-1)
        y = y[to_index(input_nodes, y.size)]
    else:
        labels = []
        for i in range(len(dataset)):
            graph = dataset[i]
            if graph.graph_labels is None:
                raise ValueError("Every graph needs `graph_labels`.")
            labels.append(to_numpy(graph.graph_labels).reshape(-1))
        y = np.concatenate(labels) if labels else np.zeros(0, dtype=np.int64)
        if y.size != len(dataset):
            raise ValueError("ImbalancedSampler requires one label per graph.")

    if y.size and not np.all(np.equal(np.mod(y, 1), 0)):
        raise ValueError("ImbalancedSampler requires integer class labels.")
    y = y.astype(np.int64)
    if y.size and y.min() < 0:
        raise ValueError("Class labels must be non-negative.")

    self.labels = y
    self.num_samples = y.size if num_samples is None else int(num_samples)
    counts = np.bincount(y) if y.size else np.zeros(0, dtype=np.int64)
    with np.errstate(divide="ignore"):
        class_weight = 1.0 / counts
    self.weight = class_weight[y]

LinkNeighborLoader(
    data: Union[GraphData, HeteroGraphData],
    num_neighbors: Union[list[int], dict[EdgeType, list[int]]],
    edge_label_index: Any = None,
    edge_label: Optional[array] = None,
    neg_sampling: Union[None, str, dict, NegativeSampling] = None,
    neg_sampling_ratio: Optional[float] = None,
    batch_size: int = 1,
    shuffle: bool = False,
    replace: bool = False,
    directed: bool = True,
    sampler: Optional[Iterable[int]] = None,
    edge_label_time: Optional[array] = None,
    time_attr: Optional[str] = None,
    temporal_strategy: str = "uniform",
    disjoint: bool = False,
)

Mini-batch loader for link-level tasks (e.g. link prediction) on a single large graph, following PyG's LinkNeighborLoader.

Iterates over the supervision edges edge_label_index. For each batch of edges (plus optional negative samples), the source and destination nodes are used as seeds of a neighbor sampling (as in NeighborLoader), and the sampled subgraph is returned with the supervision edges relabeled to local node ids.

Each batch holds, besides the sliced subgraph:

  • n_id / e_id: global ids of the sampled nodes and original ids of the sampled edges (n_id_dict / e_id_dict for heterogeneous graphs). The seed nodes come first in n_id.
  • input_id: positions in edge_label_index of the positive edges of the batch.
  • Without negative sampling, or with "binary" negative sampling: edge_label_index ([2, num_pos + num_neg], positives first, as local node ids) and edge_label (1 for positives and 0 for negatives when edge_label is not given; when edge_label is given and contains 0, it is incremented by one so that 0 means "negative").
  • With "triplet" negative sampling: src_index, dst_pos_index ([batch_size]) and dst_neg_index ([batch_size] or [batch_size, amount]), as local node ids.
  • For heterogeneous graphs: input_type, the supervised edge type. edge_label_index row 0 indexes nodes of its source type, row 1 nodes of its destination type.

Supervision edges are not removed from the message-passing graph.

Temporal sampling (homogeneous graphs), as in PyG: with time_attr and edge_label_time, the seeds of every supervision edge (and of its negatives) only sample neighbors whose timestamp is not later than the edge's time, and negatives are drawn among nodes whose timestamp is not later either (node-level time_attr). Every seed then gets its own subgraph (disjoint=True): the sources come first, then the destinations, without merging, so edge_label_index is arange(2 * num_edges).reshape(2, -1) and batch.batch holds, for every node, the position in the mini-batch of its supervision edge. Mini-batches also hold edge_label_time (seed_time for "triplet" negative sampling).

def __init__(
    self,
    data: Union[GraphData, HeteroGraphData],
    num_neighbors: Union[list[int], dict[EdgeType, list[int]]],
    edge_label_index: Any = None,
    edge_label: Optional[mx.array] = None,
    neg_sampling: Union[None, str, dict, NegativeSampling] = None,
    neg_sampling_ratio: Optional[float] = None,
    batch_size: int = 1,
    shuffle: bool = False,
    replace: bool = False,
    directed: bool = True,
    sampler: Optional[Iterable[int]] = None,
    edge_label_time: Optional[mx.array] = None,
    time_attr: Optional[str] = None,
    temporal_strategy: str = "uniform",
    disjoint: bool = False,
):
    if (edge_label_time is None) != (time_attr is None):
        raise ValueError(
            "Received conflicting 'edge_label_time' and 'time_attr' "
            "arguments: temporal sampling needs both."
        )
    if neg_sampling_ratio is not None and neg_sampling_ratio != 0.0:
        if neg_sampling is not None:
            raise ValueError(
                "Pass either `neg_sampling` or `neg_sampling_ratio`, not both."
            )
        neg_sampling = NegativeSampling("binary", neg_sampling_ratio)
    neg = NegativeSampling.cast(neg_sampling)

    if edge_label is not None and neg is not None:
        if neg.is_triplet():
            raise ValueError(
                "'edge_label' needs to be undefined for 'triplet'-based "
                "negative sampling. Use `src_index`, `dst_pos_index` and "
                "`dst_neg_index` of the returned mini-batch instead."
            )
        if edge_label.size > 0 and mx.min(edge_label).item() == 0:
            # Increment labels such that `zero` now denotes "negative".
            edge_label = edge_label + 1

    if isinstance(data, HeteroGraphData):
        if edge_label_index is None:
            raise ValueError(
                "For a HeteroGraphData, `edge_label_index` must name the "
                "supervised edge type: edge_type or (edge_type, index)."
            )
        if not directed:
            raise ValueError(
                "`directed=False` is not supported for heterogeneous graphs."
            )
        if time_attr is not None or disjoint:
            raise NotImplementedError(
                "Temporal and disjoint sampling are only supported for "
                "homogeneous graphs."
            )
        self._impl: Any = _HeteroLinkNeighborLoader(
            data,
            num_neighbors,
            edge_label_index,
            edge_label,
            neg,
            replace,
        )
    elif isinstance(data, GraphData):
        if isinstance(num_neighbors, dict):
            raise ValueError(
                "A dict of `num_neighbors` per edge type is only supported "
                "for heterogeneous graphs; pass a list for a GraphData."
            )
        self._impl = _HomogeneousLinkNeighborLoader(
            data,
            num_neighbors,
            edge_label_index,
            edge_label,
            neg,
            replace,
            directed,
            time_attr=time_attr,
            edge_label_time=edge_label_time,
            temporal_strategy=temporal_strategy,
            disjoint=disjoint,
        )
    else:
        raise TypeError(
            "`data` must be a GraphData or a HeteroGraphData, "
            f"got {type(data).__name__}."
        )

    num_label_edges = self._impl.edge_label_index.shape[1]
    if edge_label is not None and edge_label.shape[0] != num_label_edges:
        raise ValueError(
            f"`edge_label` has {edge_label.shape[0]} entries but there are "
            f"{num_label_edges} supervision edges."
        )
    if edge_label_time is not None and edge_label_time.size != num_label_edges:
        raise ValueError(
            f"`edge_label_time` has {edge_label_time.size} entries but "
            f"there are {num_label_edges} supervision edges."
        )

    self.data = data
    self.neg_sampling = neg
    self.batch_size = batch_size
    self.shuffle = shuffle
    self.sampler = sampler
    self._indices = np.arange(num_label_edges)
    self._current_index = 0

ceil(amount) negatives per seed (in blocks of one negative per seed, as in PyG), drawn among the nodes whose time is not later than the seed's when node_time is given: invalid draws are redrawn up to 5 times, then replaced by the earliest node (as in PyG).

Source code in mlx_graphs/loaders/link_neighbor_loader.py 
def sample_in_time(
    self,
    endpoint: Literal["src", "dst"],
    seed_time: np.ndarray,
    num_nodes: int,
    node_time: Optional[np.ndarray],
) -> np.ndarray:
    """``ceil(amount)`` negatives per seed (in blocks of one negative per
    seed, as in PyG), drawn among the nodes whose time is not later than
    the seed's when ``node_time`` is given: invalid draws are redrawn up
    to 5 times, then replaced by the earliest node (as in PyG)."""
    sample = self.sample_src if endpoint == "src" else self.sample_dst
    per_seed = math.ceil(self.amount)
    times = np.tile(seed_time, per_seed)
    out = sample(times.size, num_nodes)
    if node_time is None:
        return out
    invalid = np.nonzero(node_time[out] > times)[0]
    for _ in range(5):
        if invalid.size == 0:
            break
        out[invalid] = sample(invalid.size, num_nodes)
        invalid = invalid[node_time[out[invalid]] > times[invalid]]
    out[invalid] = int(np.argmin(node_time))
    return out

NeighborLoader(
    data: Union[GraphData, HeteroGraphData, tuple],
    num_neighbors: Union[list[int], dict[EdgeType, list[int]]],
    input_nodes: Union[None, array, str, tuple[str, Optional[array]]] = None,
    batch_size: int = 1,
    shuffle: bool = False,
    replace: bool = False,
    directed: bool = True,
    sampler: Optional[Iterable[int]] = None,
    time_attr: Optional[str] = None,
    input_time: Optional[array] = None,
    temporal_strategy: str = "uniform",
    disjoint: bool = False,
)

Mini-batch loader for node-level tasks on a single large graph.

Uses neighbor sampling to extract K-hop subgraphs around seed nodes. Works on both homogeneous and heterogeneous graphs, following PyG's API: the implementation is picked from the type of data.

  • GraphData: each iteration yields a GraphData holding the sampled subgraph with locally re-indexed edges.
  • HeteroGraphData: each iteration yields a HeteroGraphData with edges re-indexed locally per node type (sampled with mlx_cluster.hetero_neighbor_sample).
  • A (FeatureStore, GraphStore) pair (PyG's remote backend, see FeatureStore): the graph structure is read from the graph store, and only the rows of the sampled nodes (and edges) are gathered from the feature store at every iteration, so node features can stay on disk (MemmapFeatureStore). Store arrays named x / y / edge_attr become node_features / node_labels / edge_features of the mini-batch.

Temporal sampling (homogeneous graphs): with time_attr, only the neighbors whose timestamp is earlier than or equal to the time of their seed are sampled, as in PyG. time_attr names a node-level timestamp (the time of a neighbor is then its node's) or an edge-level one (the time of the edge, which requires input_time). The time of a seed is input_time if given, else its own node timestamp. As in PyG, every seed then gets its own subgraph (disjoint=True): a node sampled for two seeds appears twice, and batch.batch holds the position of the seed of every node. These mini-batches also hold the per-hop counts num_sampled_nodes / num_sampled_edges, and seed_time when input_time is given.

The first batch_size nodes (of the seed node type, for heterogeneous graphs) are always the seed nodes. During training, compute the loss only on these nodes:

# homogeneous
out = model(batch.node_features, batch.edge_index)
loss = loss_fn(out[: batch.batch_size], batch.node_labels[: batch.batch_size])

# heterogeneous
out = model(batch.node_features_dict, batch.edge_index_dict)
n = batch.batch_size
loss = loss_fn(out["author"][:n], batch.node_labels_dict["author"][:n])

def __init__(
    self,
    data: Union[GraphData, HeteroGraphData, tuple],
    num_neighbors: Union[list[int], dict[EdgeType, list[int]]],
    input_nodes: Union[None, mx.array, str, tuple[str, Optional[mx.array]]] = None,
    batch_size: int = 1,
    shuffle: bool = False,
    replace: bool = False,
    directed: bool = True,
    sampler: Optional[Iterable[int]] = None,
    time_attr: Optional[str] = None,
    input_time: Optional[mx.array] = None,
    temporal_strategy: str = "uniform",
    disjoint: bool = False,
):
    if isinstance(data, HeteroGraphData):
        if time_attr is not None or input_time is not None or disjoint:
            raise NotImplementedError(
                "Temporal and disjoint sampling are only supported for "
                "homogeneous graphs."
            )
        if input_nodes is None or isinstance(input_nodes, mx.array):
            raise ValueError(
                "For a HeteroGraphData, `input_nodes` must name the seed "
                "node type: 'author', ('author', indices) or "
                "('author', boolean_mask)."
            )
        if not directed:
            raise ValueError(
                "`directed=False` is not supported for heterogeneous graphs."
            )
        self._loader = _HeteroNeighborLoader(
            data,
            num_neighbors,
            input_nodes,
            batch_size=batch_size,
            shuffle=shuffle,
            replace=replace,
            sampler=sampler,
        )
    elif isinstance(data, GraphData) or is_store_pair(data):
        if isinstance(num_neighbors, dict):
            raise ValueError(
                "A dict of `num_neighbors` per edge type is only supported "
                "for heterogeneous graphs; pass a list for a GraphData."
            )
        if isinstance(input_nodes, (str, tuple)):
            raise ValueError(
                "Node types in `input_nodes` are only supported for "
                "heterogeneous graphs; pass an array of node indices "
                "for a GraphData."
            )
        self._loader = _HomogeneousNeighborLoader(
            data,
            num_neighbors,
            input_nodes,
            batch_size=batch_size,
            shuffle=shuffle,
            replace=replace,
            directed=directed,
            sampler=sampler,
            time_attr=time_attr,
            input_time=input_time,
            temporal_strategy=temporal_strategy,
            disjoint=disjoint,
        )
    else:
        raise TypeError(
            "`data` must be a GraphData or a HeteroGraphData (or a "
            f"(FeatureStore, GraphStore) pair), got {type(data).__name__}."
        )

ShaDowKHopSampler(
    data: GraphData,
    depth: int,
    num_neighbors: int,
    node_idx: Optional[Union[array, ndarray]] = None,
    replace: bool = False,
    batch_size: int = 1,
    shuffle: bool = False,

The ShaDow \(k\)-hop sampler from the "Decoupling the Depth and Scope of Graph Neural Networks" paper, following PyG's ShaDowKHopSampler.

For every seed (root) node, num_neighbors incoming neighbors are sampled per node and per hop, for depth hops, and the subgraph induced by the sampled nodes is extracted. The subgraphs of the batch_size roots of a mini-batch are kept separate (a node may appear in several of them) and returned as one block-diagonal GraphData:

  • edge_index, node- and edge-level attributes of all subgraphs, with the nodes of each subgraph sorted by global id;
  • batch_indices: subgraph of every node (PyG's batch), to pool one representation per subgraph;
  • ptr: start of every subgraph in the node list, [batch_size + 1];
  • root_n_id: position of every root node in the node list;
  • n_id / e_id: global node ids and original edge ids;
  • node_labels: like PyG's y, the labels of the roots only ([batch_size, ...]), when data.node_labels is node-level.

sample(roots: ndarray) -> GraphData

Builds the batch of the subgraphs around roots (global ids).

Source code in mlx_graphs/loaders/shadow.py 
def sample(self, roots: np.ndarray) -> GraphData:
    """Builds the batch of the subgraphs around ``roots`` (global ids)."""
    adj, N = self._adj, self.num_nodes
    num_roots = roots.size

    # Every (subgraph, node) pair is encoded as `subgraph * N + node`.
    keys = np.arange(num_roots, dtype=np.int64) * N + roots
    visited = np.unique(keys)
    frontier = keys
    for _ in range(self.depth):
        if frontier.size == 0:
            break
        owner, nbr = sample_neighbors_grouped(
            adj.colptr,
            adj.csc_row,
            frontier % N,
            self.num_neighbors,
            self.replace,
        )
        candidates = np.unique((frontier[owner] // N) * N + nbr)
        frontier = np.setdiff1d(candidates, visited, assume_unique=True)
        visited = np.union1d(visited, frontier)

    # `visited` is sorted: subgraph by subgraph, nodes by global id.
    n_id = visited % N
    batch = visited // N
    ptr = np.zeros(num_roots + 1, dtype=np.int64)
    np.cumsum(np.bincount(batch, minlength=num_roots), out=ptr[1:])
    root_n_id = np.searchsorted(visited, keys)

    # Induced subgraph of every subgraph: out-edges whose target is in it.
    starts = adj.rowptr[n_id]
    counts = adj.rowptr[n_id + 1] - starts
    pos = segment_arange(starts, counts)
    src_local = np.repeat(np.arange(n_id.size), counts)
    dst_keys = np.repeat(batch, counts) * N + adj.csr_col[pos]
    dst_local = np.searchsorted(visited, dst_keys)
    dst_local_clipped = np.minimum(dst_local, max(visited.size - 1, 0))
    keep = visited[dst_local_clipped] == dst_keys if visited.size else dst_keys[:0]
    edge_index = np.stack([src_local[keep], dst_local[keep]])
    e_id = adj.csr_perm[pos[keep]]

    out = slice_graph(
        self.data,
        n_id,
        e_id,
        edge_index,
        num_nodes=self.num_nodes,
        num_edges=self.num_edges,
        n_id=index_array(n_id, N),
        e_id=index_array(e_id, self.num_edges),
        # positions in the batch, at most num_roots * N
        batch_indices=index_array(batch, num_roots),
        ptr=index_array(ptr, visited.size + 1),
        root_n_id=index_array(root_n_id, visited.size),
    )
    labels = self.data.node_labels
    if labels is not None and labels.ndim >= 1 and labels.shape[0] == N:
        out.node_labels = labels[mx.array(roots.astype(np.int64))]
    return out

def __init__(
    self,
    data: TemporalData,
    batch_size: int = 1,
    neg_sampling_ratio: float = 0.0,
    drop_last: bool = False,
):
    if batch_size < 1:
        raise ValueError(f"`batch_size` must be positive (got {batch_size}).")
    self.data = data
    self.batch_size = batch_size
    self.events_per_batch = batch_size
    self.neg_sampling_ratio = neg_sampling_ratio
    self.drop_last = drop_last

    if neg_sampling_ratio > 0:
        self.min_dst = int(data.dst.min().item())
        self.max_dst = int(data.dst.max().item())

    num_events = len(data)
    if drop_last and num_events % batch_size != 0:
        self._starts = range(0, num_events - batch_size, batch_size)
    else:
        self._starts = range(0, num_events, batch_size)

            average during refinement. Defaults to 0.05

    Returns:
        The partition id of every node, as a ``[num_nodes]`` numpy array.
    """
    if num_parts < 1:
        raise ValueError(f"`num_parts` must be positive (got {num_parts})")
    adj = Adjacency(edge_index, num_nodes)
    rowptr, col = _symmetric_csr(adj)
    order = _bfs_order(rowptr, col)
    part = np.empty(num_nodes, dtype=np.int64)
    part[order] = (np.arange(num_nodes) * num_parts) // max(num_nodes, 1)
    if num_parts > 1 and num_iters > 0:
        part = _refine(part, rowptr, col, num_parts, num_iters, imbalance)
    return part

def __init__(
    self, metrics: Union[List[_LinkPredMetric], Dict[str, _LinkPredMetric]]
):
    if isinstance(metrics, (list, tuple)):
        metrics = {
            f"{'Weighted' if getattr(m, 'weighted', False) else ''}"
            f"{m.__class__.__name__}@{m.k}": m
            for m in metrics
        }
    if not isinstance(metrics, dict) or len(metrics) == 0:
        raise ValueError("Expected a non-empty list or dict of metrics")
    for metric in metrics.values():
        if not isinstance(metric, _LinkPredMetric):
            raise TypeError(f"'{metric}' is not a link prediction metric")
    self.metrics: Dict[str, _LinkPredMetric] = dict(metrics)

def update(
    self,
    pred_index_mat: ArrayLike,
    edge_label_index: EdgeLabelIndex,
    edge_label_weight: Optional[ArrayLike] = None,
):
    """Updates all metrics with a mini-batch of predictions (see
    :meth:`LinkPredMetric.update`). Ground-truth pairs with non-positive
    weights are dropped for all metrics, as in PyG."""
    if self.weighted and edge_label_weight is None:
        raise ValueError(
            f"'edge_label_weight' is a required argument for weighted "
            f"'{self.__class__.__name__}' metrics"
        )
    data = LinkPredMetricData(pred_index_mat, edge_label_index, edge_label_weight)
    unweighted = LinkPredMetricData(data.pred_index_mat, (data.row, data.col))
    for metric in self.metrics.values():
        if isinstance(metric, LinkPredMetric):
            metric._update(data if metric.weighted else unweighted)
        else:
            metric.update(pred_index_mat, edge_label_index, edge_label_weight)

def __init__(
    self,
    pred_index_mat: ArrayLike,
    edge_label_index: EdgeLabelIndex,
    edge_label_weight: Optional[ArrayLike] = None,
):
    self.pred_index_mat = _host(pred_index_mat).astype(np.int64)
    if self.pred_index_mat.ndim == 1:
        self.pred_index_mat = self.pred_index_mat.reshape(-1, 1)
    if isinstance(edge_label_index, (tuple, list)):
        row, col = edge_label_index
    else:
        row, col = _host(edge_label_index)
    self.row = _host(row).reshape(-1).astype(np.int64)
    self.col = _host(col).reshape(-1).astype(np.int64)
    self.edge_label_weight = None
    if edge_label_weight is not None:
        weight = _host(edge_label_weight).reshape(-1).astype(np.float64)
        pos_mask = weight > 0
        self.edge_label_weight = weight[pos_mask]
        self.row, self.col = self.row[pos_mask], self.col[pos_mask]

The evaluator of a Temporal Graph Benchmark dataset, with the same interface and results as py-tgb's Evaluator classes.

def eval(self, input_dict: dict, verbose: bool = False) -> dict:
    """Computes the metrics.

    Args:
        input_dict: The predictions (see the class description) and
            ``"eval_metric"``, a list of metric names
        verbose: Whether to print the metrics

    Returns:
        A dictionary of metric values (floats).
    """
    if "eval_metric" not in input_dict:
        raise RuntimeError("Missing key of eval_metric!")
    for metric in input_dict["eval_metric"]:
        if metric not in self.valid_metric_list:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Unsupported eval metric: {metric}, not found in "
                f"{self.valid_metric_list}"
            )

    if self.metric == "mrr":
        for key in ("y_pred_pos", "y_pred_neg"):
            if key not in input_dict:
                raise RuntimeError(f"Missing key of {key}")
        mrr, hits = tgb_mrr_hits(
            input_dict["y_pred_pos"], input_dict["y_pred_neg"], self.k_value
        )
        perf = {f"hits@{self.k_value}": hits, "mrr": mrr}
    else:
        for key in ("y_true", "y_pred"):
            if key not in input_dict:
                raise RuntimeError(f"Missing key of {key}")
        y_true = _host(input_dict["y_true"])
        y_pred = _host(input_dict["y_pred"])
        if y_true.shape != y_pred.shape:
            raise RuntimeError("Shape of y_true and y_pred must be the same!")
        perf = {}
        for metric in input_dict["eval_metric"]:
            if metric in ("mse", "rmse"):
                mse = float(np.mean((y_true - y_pred) ** 2))
                perf.update(mse=mse, rmse=math.sqrt(mse))
            elif metric == "ndcg":
                perf["ndcg"] = tgb_ndcg(y_true, y_pred, k=10)

    if verbose:
        for key, value in perf.items():
            print(f"\t>>> {key}: {value:.4f}")
    return perf

def average_precision_score(labels: ArrayLike, scores: ArrayLike) -> float:
    r"""Average precision of binary ``labels`` ranked by ``scores``.

    .. math::
        \text{AP} = \sum_n (R_n - R_{n-1}) P_n

    where :math:`P_n` and :math:`R_n` are the precision and recall at the
    :math:`n`-th distinct score threshold, as in scikit-learn's
    ``average_precision_score``.

    Args:
        labels: Binary ground truth (``1`` for positives), shape `[n]`
        scores: Scores of the samples (higher means more likely positive),
            shape `[n]`

    Returns:
        The average precision, between 0 and 1.

    Example:

    .. code-block:: python

        from mlx_graphs.metrics import average_precision_score

        average_precision_score(mx.array([1, 0, 1, 0]),
                                mx.array([0.9, 0.1, 0.4, 0.5]))
        >>> 0.8333
    """
    labels = _host(labels, np.float64)
    scores = _host(scores, np.float64)
    num_pos = labels.sum()
    if num_pos == 0:
        raise ValueError("average_precision_score needs positive samples")

    order = np.argsort(-scores, kind="mergesort")
    scores, labels = scores[order], labels[order]
    # last position of each distinct threshold
    distinct = np.where(np.diff(scores))[0]
    threshold_idx = np.r_[distinct, labels.size - 1]
    tps = np.cumsum(labels)[threshold_idx]
    precision = tps / (threshold_idx + 1)
    recall = tps / num_pos
    recall_prev = np.r_[0.0, recall[:-1]]
    return float(np.sum((recall - recall_prev) * precision))

items.text:
roc_auc_score(labels: ArrayLike, scores: ArrayLike) -> float

Area under the ROC curve of binary labels ranked by scores.

Computed with the Mann-Whitney U statistic, tied scores getting their average rank, which gives the same value as scikit-learn's roc_auc_score.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default labels ArrayLike

Binary ground truth (1 for positives), shape [n]

required scores ArrayLike

Scores of the samples (higher means more likely positive), shape [n]

required

Returns:

Type Description float

The AUC, between 0 and 1.

Example:

from mlx_graphs.metrics import roc_auc_score

roc_auc_score(mx.array([1, 0, 1, 0]), mx.array([0.9, 0.1, 0.4, 0.5]))
>>> 0.75
Source code in mlx_graphs/metrics/functional.py 
def roc_auc_score(labels: ArrayLike, scores: ArrayLike) -> float:
    """Area under the ROC curve of binary ``labels`` ranked by ``scores``.

    Computed with the Mann-Whitney U statistic, tied scores getting their
    average rank, which gives the same value as scikit-learn's
    ``roc_auc_score``.

    Args:
        labels: Binary ground truth (``1`` for positives), shape `[n]`
        scores: Scores of the samples (higher means more likely positive),
            shape `[n]`

    Returns:
        The AUC, between 0 and 1.

    Example:

    .. code-block:: python

        from mlx_graphs.metrics import roc_auc_score

        roc_auc_score(mx.array([1, 0, 1, 0]), mx.array([0.9, 0.1, 0.4, 0.5]))
        >>> 0.75
    """
    labels = _host(labels, bool)
    scores = _host(scores, np.float64)
    num_pos = int(labels.sum())
    num_neg = labels.size - num_pos
    if num_pos == 0 or num_neg == 0:
        raise ValueError("roc_auc_score needs both positive and negative samples")

    order = np.argsort(scores, kind="mergesort")
    sorted_scores = scores[order]
    ranks = np.empty(scores.size, dtype=np.float64)
    # average (1-based) rank of each group of tied scores
    _, start, counts = np.unique(sorted_scores, return_index=True, return_counts=True)
    avg_rank = start + (counts + 1) / 2.0
    ranks[order] = np.repeat(avg_rank, counts)
    sum_pos_ranks = ranks[labels].sum()
    return float((sum_pos_ranks - num_pos * (num_pos + 1) / 2.0) / (num_pos * num_neg))

MRR and Hits@k of positive scores ranked against their negative scores, as TGB.

The rank of a positive is 1 + (#negatives scoring higher + #negatives scoring at least as high) / 2: a positive tied with m negatives gets the average of its best (first) and worst (last) possible ranks among them, as TGB (and OGB). The reciprocal ranks and the hits are float32 and averaged in float32, as TGB with NumPy inputs.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default y_pred_pos ArrayLike

Score of each positive edge, shape [num_pos]

required y_pred_neg ArrayLike

Scores of the negative edges of each positive, shape [num_pos, num_neg] (or [num_neg] for a single positive). Positives with fewer negatives can be padded with -inf, which never ranks above a (finite) positive score.

required k int

The k of Hits@k. Default: 10

10

Returns:

Type Description tuple[float, float]

The mean reciprocal rank and the Hits@k.

Source code in mlx_graphs/metrics/tgb.py 
def tgb_mrr_hits(
    y_pred_pos: ArrayLike, y_pred_neg: ArrayLike, k: int = 10
) -> tuple[float, float]:
    r"""MRR and Hits@k of positive scores ranked against their negative scores,
    as TGB.

    The rank of a positive is ``1 + (#negatives scoring higher + #negatives
    scoring at least as high) / 2``: a positive tied with ``m`` negatives gets
    the average of its best (first) and worst (last) possible ranks among them,
    as TGB (and OGB). The reciprocal ranks and the hits are float32 and
    averaged in float32, as TGB with NumPy inputs.

    Args:
        y_pred_pos: Score of each positive edge, shape `[num_pos]`
        y_pred_neg: Scores of the negative edges of each positive, shape
            `[num_pos, num_neg]` (or `[num_neg]` for a single positive).
            Positives with fewer negatives can be padded with ``-inf``, which
            never ranks above a (finite) positive score.
        k: The ``k`` of Hits@k. Default: ``10``

    Returns:
        The mean reciprocal rank and the Hits@k.
    """
    y_pred_pos = _host(y_pred_pos).reshape(-1, 1)
    y_pred_neg = _host(y_pred_neg)
    optimistic_rank = (y_pred_neg > y_pred_pos).sum(axis=1)
    pessimistic_rank = (y_pred_neg >= y_pred_pos).sum(axis=1)
    ranking_list = 0.5 * (optimistic_rank + pessimistic_rank) + 1
    hits = (ranking_list <= k).astype(np.float32)
    mrr = 1.0 / ranking_list.astype(np.float32)
    return float(mrr.mean()), float(hits.mean())

tgb_ndcg(y_true: ArrayLike, y_pred: ArrayLike, k: int = 10) -> float

NDCG@k of the predicted scores of each node over the classes, averaged over the nodes, as TGB (sklearn.metrics.ndcg_score(y_true, y_pred, k=k)).

The gains are the true label weights and the discount of position i (from 0) is 1 / log2(i + 2) for the first k positions and 0 after. Tied predicted scores share the average gain of their group, and nodes whose true labels are all zero score 0.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default y_true ArrayLike

Non-negative true label weights, shape [num_nodes, num_classes]

required y_pred ArrayLike

Predicted scores, shape [num_nodes, num_classes]

required k int

Only the first k ranked classes count. Default: 10

10

Returns:

Type Description float

The mean NDCG@k.

Source code in mlx_graphs/metrics/tgb.py 
def tgb_ndcg(y_true: ArrayLike, y_pred: ArrayLike, k: int = 10) -> float:
    r"""NDCG@k of the predicted scores of each node over the classes, averaged
    over the nodes, as TGB (``sklearn.metrics.ndcg_score(y_true, y_pred,
    k=k)``).

    The gains are the true label weights and the discount of position ``i``
    (from 0) is ``1 / log2(i + 2)`` for the first ``k`` positions and 0
    after. Tied predicted scores share the average gain of their group, and
    nodes whose true labels are all zero score 0.

    Args:
        y_true: Non-negative true label weights, shape `[num_nodes, num_classes]`
        y_pred: Predicted scores, shape `[num_nodes, num_classes]`
        k: Only the first ``k`` ranked classes count. Default: ``10``

    Returns:
        The mean NDCG@k.
    """
    y_true = _host(y_true)
    y_pred = _host(y_pred)
    if y_true.shape != y_pred.shape:
        raise ValueError(
            f"y_true and y_pred must have the same shape (got {y_true.shape} "
            f"and {y_pred.shape})"
        )
    if y_true.ndim != 2 or y_true.shape[1] <= 1:
        raise ValueError(
            "Computing NDCG is only meaningful with a 2D array of more than one "
            f"class per node (got shape {y_true.shape})"
        )
    if y_true.size and y_true.min() < 0:
        raise ValueError("ndcg only supports non-negative y_true values")

    discount = 1 / (np.log(np.arange(y_true.shape[1]) + 2) / np.log(2))
    discount[k:] = 0

    discount_cumsum = np.cumsum(discount)
    gain = np.asarray(
        [
            _tie_averaged_dcg(y_t, y_s, discount_cumsum)
            for y_t, y_s in zip(y_true, y_pred)
        ]
    )
    ranking = np.argsort(y_true)[:, ::-1]
    ranked = y_true[np.arange(ranking.shape[0])[:, np.newaxis], ranking]
    normalizing_gain = discount.dot(ranked.T)

    all_irrelevant = normalizing_gain == 0
    gain[all_irrelevant] = 0
    gain[~all_irrelevant] /= normalizing_gain[~all_irrelevant]
    return float(np.average(gain))

items.text:
Layers on batched dense adjacency matrices [batch_size, num_nodes, num_nodes] (e.g. from to_dense_adj or a DenseDataLoader), called as conv(adj, node_features, mask).

items.title: Models
items.text:
Ready-to-use multi-layer models, with optional normalization, dropout and Jumping Knowledge.

Other models and building blocks:

items.title: Normalization
items.text:
Class Description BatchNormalization Applies batch normalization over a batch of features as described in the Batch Normalization: Accelerating Deep Network Training by Reducing Internal Covariate Shift" paper. HeteroBatchNormalization Applies batch normalization over a batch of heterogeneous features, as described in the "Batch Normalization: Accelerating Deep Network Training by Reducing Internal Covariate Shift" paper. PyG name Class BatchNorm BatchNormalization HeteroBatchNorm HeteroBatchNormalization InstanceNorm InstanceNormalization LayerNorm LayerNormalization HeteroLayerNorm HeteroLayerNormalization GraphNorm GraphNormalization PairNorm PairNormalization GraphSizeNorm GraphSizeNormalization MeanSubtractionNorm MeanSubtractionNormalization MessageNorm MessageNormalization DiffGroupNorm DiffGroupNormalization

items.title: Pooling and readout
items.text:
Class Description JumpingKnowledge Jumping Knowledge layer aggregation from "Representation Learning on Graphs with Jumping Knowledge Networks" paper. AttentionalAggregation Soft attention pooling (global attention) from "Gated Graph Sequence Neural Networks" paper. Set2Set Set2Set global pooling from "Order Matters: Sequence to Sequence for Sets" paper. TopKPooling \(\mathrm{top}_k\) pooling operator from the "Graph U-Nets", "Towards Sparse Hierarchical Graph Classifiers" and "Understanding Attention and Generalization in Graph Neural Networks" papers. Function Description global_add_pool() Sums all node features to obtain a global graph-level representation. global_mean_pool() Takes the feature-wise mean value along all node features to obtain a global graph-level representation. global_max_pool() Takes the feature-wise maximum value along all node features to obtain a global graph-level representation. global_sort_pool() The global pooling operator from the "An End-to-End Deep Learning Architecture for Graph Classification" paper. topk() Selects the nodes with the highest scores in each graph. filter_adj() Keeps the edges between the nodes perm, relabeled by their position in perm. knn() Finds for each point of y the k nearest points of x. knn_graph() Computes the graph connecting each point to its k nearest points. radius() Finds for each point of y the points of x within distance r. radius_graph() Computes the graph connecting each point to the points within distance r.

Point cloud sampling and cluster pooling (fps, voxel_grid, graclus and nearest are also in mlx_graphs.utils):

Function Description fps() Farthest point sampling, from the "PointNet++: Deep Hierarchical Feature Learning on Point Sets in a Metric Space" paper. voxel_grid() Voxel grid pooling from the "Dynamic Edge-Conditioned Filters in Convolutional Networks on Graphs" paper: overlays a regular grid of user-defined size over a point cloud and clusters all the points within the same voxel. graclus() A greedy clustering algorithm from the "Weighted Graph Cuts without Eigenvectors: A Multilevel Approach" paper, which matches each node with one of its unmarked neighbors (the one maximizing the edge weight, if given). nearest() Assigns each point of x to its nearest point of y, in the same graph. avg_pool() Pools and coarsens a graph given by a clustering, averaging the node features and the positions of each cluster (as PyG's avg_pool). max_pool() Pools and coarsens a graph given by a clustering, taking the feature-wise maximum of the nodes of each cluster (as PyG's max_pool). avg_pool_x() Averages the features of the nodes of each cluster. max_pool_x() Takes the feature-wise maximum of the nodes of each cluster.

items.title: Hierarchical and dense pooling

Dense pooling learns soft cluster assignments on dense batched graphs and returns auxiliary losses; sparse hierarchical pooling coarsens a batch of graphs given by edge_index and batch_indices.

PANPooling The path integral based pooling operator from the "Path Integral Based Convolution and Pooling for Graph Neural Networks" paper. PANConv The path integral based convolutional operator from the "Path Integral Based Convolution and Pooling for Graph Neural Networks" paper. items.title: Aggregations
items.text:
Aggregation operators of mlx_graphs.nn.aggr (as torch_geometric.nn.aggr). They reduce a set of elements given by an index (aggr(x, index, dim_size)) and can be used as readouts, or passed as aggr to any MessagePassing layer, alone or as a list (e.g. SAGEConv(16, 32, aggr=["mean", "max"])).

Class Description Aggregation Base class of the aggregation operators, mirroring torch_geometric.nn.aggr.Aggregation. SumAggregation Sums the elements of each set. MeanAggregation Averages the elements of each set. MaxAggregation Feature-wise maximum of the elements of each set (0 for empty sets). MinAggregation Feature-wise minimum of the elements of each set (0 for empty sets). MulAggregation Feature-wise product of the elements of each set (1 for empty sets). VarAggregation Feature-wise (population) variance of the elements of each set. StdAggregation Feature-wise (population) standard deviation of the elements of each set. SoftmaxAggregation Softmax aggregation with an (optionally learnable) inverse temperature, from "DeeperGCN: All You Need to Train Deeper GCNs" paper. PowerMeanAggregation Power mean aggregation with an (optionally learnable) power, from "DeeperGCN: All You Need to Train Deeper GCNs" paper. MedianAggregation Feature-wise median of the elements of each set. QuantileAggregation Feature-wise \(q\)-th quantile of the elements of each set. MultiAggregation Applies several aggregations and combines their results, as in "Principal Neighbourhood Aggregation for Graph Nets" and "Adaptive Filters and Aggregator Fusion for Efficient Graph Convolutions" papers. DegreeScalerAggregation Combines one or more aggregations and rescales their output with one or more degree-based scalers, from "Principal Neighbourhood Aggregation for Graph Nets" paper. SortAggregation Sort pooling from "An End-to-End Deep Learning Architecture for Graph Classification" paper (DGCNN). DeepSetsAggregation Deep Sets aggregation: the elements are transformed by a network \(\phi_{\mathbf{\Theta}}\), summed, and the sum is transformed by a network \(\rho_{\mathbf{\Theta}}\), as in "Graph Neural Networks with Adaptive Readouts" paper. LSTMAggregation Aggregation with an LSTM, from the "Inductive Representation Learning on Large Graphs" paper, as PyG's LSTMAggregation. GRUAggregation Aggregation with a GRU, from the "Graph Neural Networks with Adaptive Readouts" paper, as PyG's GRUAggregation. SetTransformerAggregation Aggregation with a Set Transformer, from the "Set Transformer: A Framework for Attention-based Permutation-Invariant Neural Networks" paper, as PyG's SetTransformerAggregation. GraphMultisetTransformer The Graph Multiset Transformer pooling operator from the "Accurate Learning of Graph Representations with Graph Multiset Pooling" paper, as PyG's GraphMultisetTransformer. MLPAggregation Aggregation with a multi-layer perceptron on the concatenated elements of each set, from the "Graph Neural Networks with Adaptive Readouts" paper, as PyG's MLPAggregation. LCMAggregation The Learnable Commutative Monoid aggregation from the "Learnable Commutative Monoids for Graph Neural Networks" paper, as PyG's LCMAggregation. EquilibriumAggregation The equilibrium aggregation layer from the "Equilibrium Aggregation: Encoding Sets via Optimization" paper, as PyG's EquilibriumAggregation. VariancePreservingAggregation The variance-preserving aggregation from the "GNN-VPA: A Variance-Preserving Aggregation Strategy for Graph Neural Networks" paper, as in PyG.

Set transformer building blocks:

Class Description MultiheadAttentionBlock The Multihead Attention Block (MAB) from the "Set Transformer: A Framework for Attention-based Permutation-Invariant Neural Networks" paper, as in PyG. SetAttentionBlock The Set Attention Block (SAB) from the "Set Transformer" paper: \(\mathrm{SAB}(\mathbf{X}) = \mathrm{MAB}(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y})\). InducedSetAttentionBlock The Induced Set Attention Block (ISAB) from the "Set Transformer" paper: \(\mathrm{ISAB}(\mathbf{X}) = \mathrm{MAB}(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{h})\) with \(\mathbf{h} = \mathrm{MAB}(\mathbf{I}, \mathbf{x})\) for learnable induced points \(\mathbf{I}\). PoolingByMultiheadAttention The Pooling by Multihead Attention (PMA) layer from the "Set Transformer" paper: \(\mathrm{PMA}(\mathbf{X}) = \mathrm{MAB}(\mathbf{S}, \mathrm{ReLU}(\mathbf{X}\mathbf{W}))\) for learnable seed points \(\mathbf{S}\).

Dense layout of grouped elements (used by the set and graph transformers):

Class Description DenseLayout Host-side layout of a set of elements grouped by index into a dense [num_sets, max_set_size, ...] array, as PyG's to_dense_batch. Function Description aggregation_resolver() Returns the Aggregation described by aggr, as PyG's aggregation_resolver.

items.title: Positional encodings
items.text:
Encodings of positions and times (torch_geometric.nn.encoding), and the projections of the random-walk / Laplacian positional encodings used by graph transformers such as GPSConv.

Class Description PositionalEncoding The sinusoidal positional encoding from the "Attention Is All You Need" paper, as PyG's PositionalEncoding. TemporalEncoding The time encoding from the "Do We Really Need Complicated Model Architectures for Temporal Networks?" paper, as PyG's TemporalEncoding. RWSEEncoder Projection of the random-walk structural encodings (RWSE) of the nodes, as in the GPS example of PyG (examples/graph_gps.py) and the RWSE node encoder of GraphGPS. LapPEEncoder Projection of the Laplacian eigenvector positional encodings (LapPE) of the nodes, as the linear LapPE node encoder of GraphGPS.

items.title: Attention
items.text:
Global attention mechanisms of mlx_graphs.nn.attention (as torch_geometric.nn.attention), applied to dense batches of node features [batch_size, num_nodes, channels] with a mask of the real nodes. They are also exported by mlx_graphs.nn, as in PyG.

Class Description MultiheadAttention Multi-head scaled dot-product attention with the semantics of torch.nn.MultiheadAttention(..., batch_first=True). PerformerAttention The linear scaled attention mechanism from the "Rethinking Attention with Performers" paper, as in PyG. SGFormerAttention The simple global attention mechanism from the "SGFormer: Simplifying and Empowering Transformers for Large-Graph Representations" paper, as in PyG. PolynormerAttention The polynomial-expressive linear global attention from the "Polynormer: Polynomial-Expressive Graph Transformer in Linear Time" paper, as in PyG.

items.title: Fused message passing
items.text:
Layers decorated with fused_message_passing() aggregate neighbours with a single sparse-dense matmul (SpMM) from mlx-cluster instead of gather-scatter, so the [num_edges, features] message array is never created. GCNConv, SAGEConv, GINConv, GATConv, GATv2Conv, GraphConv, SGConv, APPNP, ChebConv, TAGConv and SimpleConv use it out of the box (the attention layers aggregate with one SpMM per head). Layers whose messages can't be fused (e.g. GINE with edge features) fall back to gather-scatter automatically.

The default format="auto" starts with the COO kernel and switches to the faster, deterministic CSR kernel once converting the graph pays off: right away for graphs with a million edges or more, and after a few calls on the same edge_index otherwise (e.g. full-batch training). Conversions are cached by edge_index identity; call clear_csr_cache() after modifying an edge_index in place.

import mlx_graphs.nn as gnn

# Turn it off globally, or force a format for every layer
gnn.set_fused_message_passing(True, format="csr")

# Or only for a block of code (handy for comparing both paths)
with gnn.fused_message_passing_mode(False):
    reference = model(edge_index, x)
Function Description fused_message_passing() Class decorator: lets a MessagePassing layer fuse message and aggregate into a single sparse x dense matmul (SpMM). set_fused_message_passing() Globally enables/disables fused message passing. fused_message_passing_mode() Context manager version of set_fused_message_passing(). is_fused_message_passing_enabled() Whether fused message passing is enabled and the kernels are available. clear_csr_cache() Drops all cached CSR conversions used by the "auto" and "csr" formats of fused message passing. gcn_norm() Symmetric GCN normalization of a graph. clear_norm_cache() Drops the cached graph normalizations.

items.title: Temporal graph networks
items.text:
The TGN memory model and its building blocks (mlx_graphs.nn.models.tgn, as torch_geometric.nn.models.tgn). See examples/tgn_jodie.py.

Class Description TGNMemory The Temporal Graph Network (TGN) memory model from the "Temporal Graph Networks for Deep Learning on Dynamic Graphs" paper, as PyG's torch_geometric.nn.TGNMemory. Class Description IdentityMessage The identity message function of TGN: the concatenation of the source and destination memories, the raw message and the time encoding. LastAggregator Keeps, for every node, the message with the latest timestamp (the message stored last among equal timestamps). MeanAggregator Averages the messages of every node (zeros for nodes without messages). TimeEncoder The time encoder of TGN, \(\cos(\mathbf{w} t + \mathbf{b})\). GRUCell A gated recurrent unit cell with the parameters and initialization of torch.nn.GRUCell. LastNeighborLoader Keeps, for every node, its size most recent neighbors in an ever-growing (undirected) temporal graph, as PyG's torch_geometric.nn.models.tgn.LastNeighborLoader.

items.title: Heterogeneous models
items.text:
to_hetero() converts a homogeneous model (e.g. a GraphSAGE, or a model written with message passing layers, Linear layers and activations) into a heterogeneous one, with one copy of every message passing layer per edge type and of every other layer per node type, like PyG's to_hetero. The converted model takes dicts keyed by node and edge types.

from mlx_graphs.nn import GraphSAGE, to_hetero

model = to_hetero(
    GraphSAGE(64, 64, num_layers=2, out_features_dim=4),
    data.metadata(),
    input_dims=data.num_node_features,  # no lazy sizes in MLX
)
out = model(data.edge_index_dict, data.node_features_dict)
Name Description to_hetero() Conversion of homogeneous GNN models into heterogeneous ones (to_hetero). to_hetero_with_bases() Converts a homogeneous GNN model into its heterogeneous equivalent via the basis-decomposition technique of the "Modeling Relational Data with Graph Convolutional Networks" paper (PyG's to_hetero_with_bases). ToHeteroModel Heterogeneous version of a homogeneous model, returned by to_hetero().

items.title: AGNNConv
items.text:
AGNNConv(requires_grad: bool = True, add_self_loops: bool = True, **kwargs)

Bases: MessagePassing

Graph attentional propagation layer from the "Attention-based Graph Neural Network for Semi-Supervised Learning" paper.

\[ \mathbf{H} = \mathbf{P} \mathbf{X}, \]

where the propagation matrix \(\mathbf{P}\) is computed as

\[ P_{i,j} = \frac{\exp( \beta \cdot \cos(\mathbf{x}_i, \mathbf{x}_j))} {\sum_{k \in \mathcal{N}(i)\cup \{ i \}} \exp( \beta \cdot \cos(\mathbf{x}_i, \mathbf{x}_k))} \]

with a (trainable) temperature \(\beta\). The layer keeps the size of the node features.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default requires_grad bool

Whether \(\beta\) is trainable (it is fixed to 1 otherwise). Default: True

True add_self_loops bool

Whether to replace the self-loops of the graph by one self-loop per node. Default: True

True **kwargs

Arguments of MessagePassing

{}

Example:

import mlx.core as mx
from mlx_graphs.nn import AGNNConv

edge_index = mx.array([[0, 1, 2, 3, 4], [1, 0, 3, 2, 0]])
node_features = mx.random.normal((5, 16))

conv = AGNNConv()
h = conv(edge_index, node_features)
>>> h.shape
(5, 16)

def __init__(
    self, requires_grad: bool = True, add_self_loops: bool = True, **kwargs
):
    kwargs.setdefault("aggr", "add")
    super(AGNNConv, self).__init__(**kwargs)

    self.requires_grad = requires_grad
    self._add_self_loops = add_self_loops
    self.beta = mx.ones((1,))
    if not requires_grad:
        self.freeze(keys=["beta"], recurse=False)

def __call__(self, edge_index: mx.array, node_features: mx.array) -> mx.array:
    """Computes the forward pass of AGNNConv.

    Args:
        edge_index: Input edge index of shape `[2, num_edges]`
        node_features: Input node features

    Returns:
        mx.array: The computed node embeddings
    """
    num_nodes = node_features.shape[0]
    src, dst = edge_index[0], edge_index[1]
    # Cosine similarity, with PyG's F.normalize epsilon.
    # p_norm: zero gradient for nodes whose features are all zero
    norm = p_norm(node_features, axis=-1, keepdims=True)
    x_norm = node_features / mx.maximum(norm, 1e-12)
    alpha = self.beta * (x_norm[src] * x_norm[dst]).sum(-1)

    if self._add_self_loops:
        # Existing self-loops are masked out of the softmax (instead of
        # being removed, which would need a data-dependent shape), and one
        # self-loop per node is appended.
        alpha = mx.where(src == dst, -float("inf"), alpha)
        loop_alpha = self.beta * (x_norm * x_norm).sum(-1)
        alpha = mx.concatenate([alpha, loop_alpha])
        loop = mx.arange(num_nodes, dtype=edge_index.dtype)
        edge_index = mx.concatenate([edge_index, mx.stack([loop, loop])], axis=1)

    alpha = scatter(alpha, edge_index[1], num_nodes, aggr="softmax")

    return self.propagate(
        edge_index=edge_index,
        node_features=node_features,
        message_kwargs={"edge_weights": alpha},
    )

items.text:
APPNP(
    K: int,
    alpha: float,
    dropout: float = 0.0,
    add_self_loops: bool = True,
    **kwargs,
)

Bases: MessagePassing

Approximate personalized propagation of neural predictions layer from "Predict then Propagate: Graph Neural Networks meet Personalized PageRank" paper.

\[ \mathbf{X}^{(0)} &= \mathbf{X} \mathbf{X}^{(k)} &= (1 - \alpha) \mathbf{\hat{D}}^{-1/2} \mathbf{\hat{A}} \mathbf{\hat{D}}^{-1/2} \mathbf{X}^{(k-1)} + \alpha \mathbf{X}^{(0)} \mathbf{H} &= \mathbf{X}^{(K)}, \]

where \(\mathbf{\hat{A}} = \mathbf{A} + \mathbf{I}\) is the (weighted) adjacency matrix with self-loops and \(\mathbf{\hat{D}}\) its diagonal degree matrix.

The layer has no parameters. It is usually applied to the output of an MLP.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default K int

Number of propagation steps

required alpha float

Teleport probability \(\alpha\)

required dropout float

Probability to drop each edge of the normalized adjacency matrix. A new set of edges is dropped at every propagation step, and only in training mode.

0.0 add_self_loops bool

Whether to add a self-loop to every node that has none

True **kwargs

Arguments of MessagePassing

{}

import mlx.core as mx
import mlx.nn as nn
from mlx_graphs.nn import APPNP

edge_index = mx.array([[0, 1, 2, 3, 4], [0, 0, 1, 1, 3]])
node_features = mx.ones((5, 16))

mlp = nn.Linear(16, 32)
prop = APPNP(K=10, alpha=0.1)
h = prop(edge_index, mlp(node_features))
>>> h.shape

def __init__(
    self,
    K: int,
    alpha: float,
    dropout: float = 0.0,
    add_self_loops: bool = True,
    **kwargs,
):
    kwargs.setdefault("aggr", "add")
    super(APPNP, self).__init__(**kwargs)

    if not 0.0 <= dropout < 1.0:
        raise ValueError(f"dropout must be in [0, 1), got {dropout}")

    self.K = K
    self.alpha = alpha
    self.dropout = dropout
    self._add_self_loops = add_self_loops

def __call__(
    self,
    edge_index: mx.array,
    node_features: mx.array,
    edge_weights: Optional[mx.array] = None,
) -> mx.array:
    """Computes the forward pass of APPNP.

    Args:
        edge_index: Input edge index of shape `[2, num_edges]`
        node_features: Input node features
        edge_weights: Optional scalar weight per edge, of shape `[num_edges]`
            or `[num_edges, 1]`. Default: ``None``

    Returns:
        mx.array: The propagated node features, same shape as ``node_features``
    """
    edge_index, norm = cached_gcn_norm(
        edge_index,
        node_features.shape[0],
        edge_weights,
        add_self_loops=self._add_self_loops,
    )

    keep_prob = 1.0 - self.dropout
    initial_features = node_features
    for _ in range(self.K):
        step_norm = norm
        if self.training and self.dropout > 0:
            keep = mx.random.bernoulli(keep_prob, norm.shape)
            step_norm = norm * keep / keep_prob

        node_features = self.propagate(
            edge_index=edge_index,
            node_features=node_features,
            message_kwargs={"edge_weights": step_norm},
        )
        node_features = (
            1 - self.alpha
        ) * node_features + self.alpha * initial_features

    return node_features

def reg_loss(self, z: mx.array) -> mx.array:
    """Regularization loss of the encoder: fooling the discriminator.

    Args:
        z: The latent space :math:`\\mathbf{Z}`
    """
    real = mx.sigmoid(self.discriminator(z))
    return -mx.log(real + EPS).mean()

def discriminator_loss(self, z: mx.array) -> mx.array:
    """Loss of the discriminator, telling Gaussian samples (real) from
    latent embeddings (fake). No gradient flows into ``z``.

    Args:
        z: The latent space :math:`\\mathbf{Z}`
    """
    real = mx.sigmoid(self.discriminator(mx.random.normal(z.shape)))
    fake = mx.sigmoid(self.discriminator(mx.stop_gradient(z)))
    real_loss = -mx.log(real + EPS).mean()
    fake_loss = -mx.log(1 - fake + EPS).mean()
    return real_loss + fake_loss

ARMAConv(

    out_features_dim: int,

Bases: MessagePassing

ARMA graph convolution layer from the "Graph Neural Networks with Convolutional ARMA Filters" paper.

\[ \mathbf{H} = \frac{1}{K} \sum_{k=1}^K \mathbf{X}_k^{(T)}, \]

where each of the \(K\) stacks is computed recursively by

\[ \mathbf{X}_k^{(t+1)} = \sigma \left( \mathbf{\hat{L}} \mathbf{X}_k^{(t)} \mathbf{W} + \mathbf{X}^{(0)} \mathbf{V} \right), \]

with \(\mathbf{\hat{L}} = \mathbf{I} - \mathbf{L} = \mathbf{D}^{-1/2} \mathbf{A} \mathbf{D}^{-1/2}\) (no self-loops are added) and \(\mathbf{X}_k^{(0)} = \mathbf{X}\).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default node_features_dim int

Size of input node features

required out_features_dim int

Size of output node embeddings

required num_stacks int

Number of parallel stacks \(K\). Default: 1

1 num_layers int

Number of layers \(T\) of each stack. Default: 1

1 shared_weights bool

If True, all layers of a stack share their weights. Default: False

False act Optional[Callable[[array], array]]

Activation function \(\sigma\) applied after each layer, or None. Default: mlx.nn.relu()

relu dropout float

Dropout probability of the skip connection \(\mathbf{X}^{(0)}\), applied in training mode. Default: 0

0.0 bias bool

Whether to add a bias after each layer. Default: True

True **kwargs

{}

node_features = mx.random.normal((5, 16))

def __init__(
    self,
    node_features_dim: int,
    out_features_dim: int,
    num_stacks: int = 1,
    num_layers: int = 1,
    shared_weights: bool = False,
    act: Optional[Callable[[mx.array], mx.array]] = nn.relu,
    dropout: float = 0.0,
    bias: bool = True,
    **kwargs,
):
    kwargs.setdefault("aggr", "add")
    super(ARMAConv, self).__init__(**kwargs)

    self.node_features_dim = node_features_dim
    self.out_features_dim = out_features_dim
    self.num_stacks = num_stacks
    self.num_layers = num_layers
    self.shared_weights = shared_weights
    self.act = act

    K, F_in, F_out = num_stacks, node_features_dim, out_features_dim
    T = 1 if shared_weights else num_layers

    # Same shapes as PyG.
    self.weight = glorot((max(1, T - 1), K, F_out, F_out))
    self.init_weight = glorot((K, F_in, F_out))
    self.root_weight = glorot((T, K, F_in, F_out))
    if bias:
        self.bias = mx.zeros((T, K, 1, F_out))
    if dropout > 0:
        self.dropout = nn.Dropout(dropout)

def __call__(
    self,
    edge_index: mx.array,
    node_features: mx.array,
    edge_weights: Optional[mx.array] = None,
) -> mx.array:
    """Computes the forward pass of ARMAConv.

    Args:
        edge_index: Input edge index of shape `[2, num_edges]`
        node_features: Input node features
        edge_weights: Optional scalar weight per edge, of shape `[num_edges]`
            or `[num_edges, 1]`. Default: ``None``

    Returns:
        mx.array: The computed node embeddings
    """
    num_nodes = node_features.shape[0]
    K, F_out = self.num_stacks, self.out_features_dim
    edge_index, norm = cached_gcn_norm(
        edge_index, num_nodes, edge_weights, add_self_loops=False
    )

    # Stacks are kept in a [num_nodes, K, F] layout, and flattened to
    # [num_nodes, K * F] for message passing.
    out = node_features
    for t in range(self.num_layers):
        if t == 0:
            out = mx.einsum("nf,kfo->nko", out, self.init_weight)
        else:
            weight = self.weight[0 if self.shared_weights else t - 1]
            out = mx.einsum("nkf,kfo->nko", out, weight)

        out = self.propagate(
            edge_index=edge_index,
            node_features=out.reshape(num_nodes, K * F_out),
            message_kwargs={"edge_weights": norm},
        ).reshape(num_nodes, K, F_out)

        root = node_features
        if "dropout" in self:
            root = self.dropout(root)
        root_weight = self.root_weight[0 if self.shared_weights else t]
        out = out + mx.einsum("nf,kfo->nko", root, root_weight)

        if "bias" in self:
            out = out + self.bias[0 if self.shared_weights else t][:, 0]
        if self.act is not None:
            out = self.act(out)

    return out.mean(axis=1)

items.title: ASAPooling
items.text:
ASAPooling(
    node_features_dim: int,
    ratio: Union[float, int] = 0.5,
    GNN: Optional[Callable[..., Module]] = None,
    dropout: float = 0.0,
    negative_slope: float = 0.2,
    add_self_loops: bool = False,
    **kwargs,
)

Bases: Module

The Adaptive Structure Aware Pooling operator from the "ASAP: Adaptive Structure Aware Pooling for Learning Hierarchical Graph Representations" paper.

Every node \(i\) defines a cluster made of its 1-hop neighbourhood (and itself). The cluster representation is an attention-weighted sum of the features of its members, where the attention (a softmax over the members) compares each member with a master query (the feature-wise maximum of the members). The clusters with the best fitness (a sigmoid of an LEConv layer) are kept, scaled by their fitness, and the pooled adjacency is \(\mathbf{S}^{\top} \mathbf{A} \mathbf{S}\), where \(\mathbf{S}\) holds the attention scores of the kept clusters.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default node_features_dim int

Size of the input node features.

required ratio Union[float, int]

The graph pooling ratio, used to compute \(k = \lceil \mathrm{ratio} \cdot N \rceil\) for a float, or \(k\) itself for an integer. Default: 0.5

0.5 GNN Optional[Callable[..., Module]]

Optional class of a graph neural network layer computing the features used by the attention, created as GNN(node_features_dim, node_features_dim, **kwargs) and called as gnn(edge_index, node_features, edge_weights) (e.g. GraphConv). Default: None

None dropout float

Dropout probability of the attention scores. Default: 0.0

0.0 negative_slope float

Negative slope of the leaky ReLU of the attention. Default: 0.2

0.2 add_self_loops bool

Whether to add a self-loop to every pooled node (the pooled self-loops are removed otherwise). Default: False

False **kwargs

Additional arguments of GNN.

{}

Example:

import mlx.core as mx
from mlx_graphs.nn import ASAPooling

pool = ASAPooling(16, ratio=0.5)
edge_index = mx.array([[0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 4], [1, 0, 2, 1, 4, 3]])
node_features = mx.random.normal((5, 16))
batch_indices = mx.array([0, 0, 0, 1, 1])

x, edge_index, edge_weights, batch_indices, perm = pool(
    edge_index, node_features, batch_indices=batch_indices

def __call__(
    self,
    edge_index: mx.array,
    node_features: mx.array,
    edge_weights: Optional[mx.array] = None,
    batch_indices: Optional[mx.array] = None,
) -> Tuple[mx.array, mx.array, Optional[mx.array], mx.array, mx.array]:
    """Pools the graphs.

    Args:
        edge_index: Edges of shape ``[2, num_edges]``.
        node_features: Node features of shape ``[num_nodes,
            node_features_dim]``.
        edge_weights: Optional weight of each edge, of shape
            ``[num_edges]``. Default: ``None``
        batch_indices: Graph of each node, of shape ``[num_nodes]``.
            Default: ``None`` (a single graph).

    Returns:
        A tuple ``(node_features, edge_index, edge_weights, batch_indices,
        perm)`` with the pooled graph (``edge_weights`` is ``None`` if it
        was not given) and the indices ``perm`` of the kept clusters.
    """
    x = node_features
    num_nodes = x.shape[0]
    if edge_weights is not None:
        edge_weights = edge_weights.reshape(-1)
    edge_index, edge_weights = add_remaining_self_loops(
        edge_index, edge_weights, fill_value=1.0, num_nodes=num_nodes
    )
    if batch_indices is None:
        batch_indices = mx.zeros((num_nodes,), dtype=mx.int32)
    if x.ndim == 1:
        x = x[:, None]
    src, dst = edge_index[0], edge_index[1]

    x_pool = x
    if "gnn_intra_cluster" in self:
        x_pool = self.gnn_intra_cluster(edge_index, x, edge_weights)

    x_pool_j = x_pool[src]
    x_q = scatter(x_pool_j, dst, num_nodes, "max")
    x_q = self.lin(x_q)[dst]

    score = self.att(mx.concatenate([x_q, x_pool_j], axis=-1)).reshape(-1)
    score = nn.leaky_relu(score, self.negative_slope)
    score = scatter_softmax(score, dst, num_nodes)
    if self.dropout is not None:
        score = self.dropout(score)

    x = scatter(x[src] * score[:, None], dst, num_nodes, "add")

    # Cluster selection.
    fitness = mx.sigmoid(self.gnn_score(edge_index, x)).reshape(-1)
    perm, _ = self.select(fitness, batch_indices)
    x = x[perm] * fitness[perm][:, None]
    batch_indices = batch_indices[perm]

    # Graph coarsening: S^T A S, with S [num_nodes, num_kept] the
    # attention scores of the kept clusters.
    edges = _to_numpy(edge_index).astype(np.int64)
    kept = _to_numpy(perm).astype(np.int64)
    position = np.full(num_nodes, -1, dtype=np.int64)
    position[kept] = np.arange(kept.size)
    in_s = np.nonzero(position[edges[1]] >= 0)[0]
    s_index = mx.array(
        np.stack([edges[0][in_s], position[edges[1][in_s]]]).astype(np.int32)
    )
    s_value = score[mx.array(in_s.astype(np.int32))]

    a_s_index, a_s_value = spspmm(
        edge_index, edge_weights, s_index, s_value, kept.size
    )
    new_index, new_value = spspmm(
        transpose(s_index), s_value, a_s_index, a_s_value, kept.size
    )

    new_weights = new_value if edge_weights is not None else None
    if self.add_self_loops:
        # the pooled self-loops keep their weight
        new_index, new_weights = add_remaining_self_loops(
            new_index, new_weights, num_nodes=kept.size
        )
    else:
        new_edges = _to_numpy(new_index)
        not_loop = np.nonzero(new_edges[0] != new_edges[1])[0]
        new_index = mx.array(new_edges[:, not_loop].astype(np.int32))
        if new_weights is not None:
            new_weights = new_weights[mx.array(not_loop.astype(np.int32))]

    return x, new_index, new_weights, batch_indices, perm

items.title: Aggregation
items.text:
Bases: Module

Base class of the aggregation operators, mirroring torch_geometric.nn.aggr.Aggregation.

An aggregation reduces a set of elements (e.g. the messages received by each node, or the nodes of each graph) to a single vector per set. The sets are given by an index array mapping every element of x to its set, and the reduction is always done along the first axis of x:

x = mx.random.normal((10, 64))
index = mx.array([0, 0, 1, 0, 2, 0, 2, 1, 0, 2])

out = aggr(x, index)  # shape [3, 64]

index does not need to be sorted. Unlike PyG, compressed ptr inputs and a dim argument are not supported: elements are always stacked along axis 0, which is the mlx-graphs convention.

Aggregations can be used on their own (e.g. as a global readout with index = batch_indices) or passed as aggr to any MessagePassing layer.

Subclasses implement aggregate(), which receives a validated index and dim_size.

def __call__(
    self,
    x: mx.array,
    index: Optional[mx.array] = None,
    dim_size: Optional[int] = None,
    **kwargs: Any,
) -> mx.array:
    """Aggregates the elements of ``x`` according to ``index``.

    Args:
        x: Array of shape ``[num_elements, ...]`` with the elements to
            aggregate (e.g. messages or node features).
        index: Array of shape ``[num_elements]`` with the set of each
            element (e.g. the destination node of each message, or
            ``batch_indices``). If ``None``, all the elements form a
            single set.
        dim_size: Number of sets, i.e. size of the first axis of the
            output. Defaults to ``index.max() + 1`` (``1`` without
            ``index``).
        **kwargs: Additional arguments of the aggregation.

    Returns:
        An array of shape ``[dim_size, ...]``.
    """
    if x.ndim == 0:
        raise ValueError("Aggregations need at least a one-dimensional input")
    if index is None:
        index = mx.zeros((x.shape[0],), dtype=mx.int32)
        dim_size = 1 if dim_size is None else dim_size
    elif dim_size is None:
        dim_size = int(index.max().item()) + 1 if index.size > 0 else 0
    return self.aggregate(x, index, dim_size, **kwargs)

Bases: Module

Soft attention pooling (global attention) from "Gated Graph Sequence Neural Networks" paper.

\[ \mathbf{r}_g = \sum_{i \in \mathcal{V}_g} \textrm{softmax}_{i \in \mathcal{V}_g} \left( h_{\textrm{gate}} ( \mathbf{x}_i ) \right) \cdot h_{\mathbf{\Theta}} ( \mathbf{x}_i ), \]

where \(\mathcal{V}_g\) are the nodes of graph \(g\), \(h_{\textrm{gate}}\) (gate_nn) computes the attention scores and \(h_{\mathbf{\Theta}}\) (nn) optionally transforms the node features before pooling.

def __call__(
    self,
    node_features: mx.array,
    batch_indices: Optional[mx.array] = None,
    num_graphs: Optional[int] = None,
) -> mx.array:
    """Pools the node features of each graph with attention.

    Args:
        node_features: Node features array.
        batch_indices: Batch array of shape (node_features.shape[0]),
            indicating for each node its batch index. If not provided, all
            nodes belong to a single graph.
        num_graphs: Number of graphs in the batch. By default, inferred as
            ``batch_indices.max() + 1``.

    Returns:
        An array of shape (num_graphs, out_features_dim) with the pooled
        features of each graph, (1, out_features_dim) if `batch_indices` is
        None. Graphs without nodes get zeros.
    """
    if batch_indices is None:
        batch_indices = mx.zeros((node_features.shape[0],), dtype=mx.int32)
        num_graphs = 1
    elif num_graphs is None:
        num_graphs = batch_indices.max().item() + 1

    gate = self.gate_nn(node_features)
    if "nn" in self:
        node_features = self.nn(node_features)

    # softmax over the nodes of each graph
    gate = scatter(gate, batch_indices, num_graphs, aggr="softmax")

    return scatter(gate * node_features, batch_indices, num_graphs, aggr="add")

Bases: Module

The Attentive FP model for molecular representation learning from the "Pushing the Boundaries of Molecular Representation for Drug Discovery with the Graph Attention Mechanism" paper, based on graph attention mechanisms.

Atom embeddings are updated by graph attention layers (a GATEConv using the bond features, then GATConv layers) followed by GRU cells; the molecule embedding is then refined for num_timesteps steps by attending over the atoms of the molecule (a GAT layer from the atoms to a virtual molecule node, followed by a GRU cell).

The model follows PyG's AttentiveFP (same arguments, parameters and initialization).

def __init__(
    self,
    in_channels: int,
    hidden_channels: int,
    out_channels: int,
    edge_dim: int,
    num_layers: int,
    num_timesteps: int,
    dropout: float = 0.0,
):
    super().__init__()
    self.in_channels = in_channels
    self.hidden_channels = hidden_channels
    self.out_channels = out_channels
    self.edge_dim = edge_dim
    self.num_layers = num_layers
    self.num_timesteps = num_timesteps

    # initialized like torch.nn.Linear (PyG's default Linear initializer)
    self.lin1 = nn.Linear(in_channels, hidden_channels)
    self.gate_conv = GATEConv(hidden_channels, hidden_channels, edge_dim, dropout)
    self.gru = GRUCell(hidden_channels, hidden_channels)

    self.atom_convs = [
        GATConv(
            hidden_channels,
            hidden_channels,
            dropout=dropout,
            add_self_loops=False,
            negative_slope=0.01,
        )
        for _ in range(num_layers - 1)
    ]
    self.atom_grus = [
        GRUCell(hidden_channels, hidden_channels) for _ in range(num_layers - 1)
    ]
    self.mol_conv = GATConv(
        hidden_channels,
        hidden_channels,
        dropout=dropout,
        add_self_loops=False,
        negative_slope=0.01,
    )
    self.mol_gru = GRUCell(hidden_channels, hidden_channels)
    self.lin2 = nn.Linear(hidden_channels, out_channels)
    self.dropout = nn.Dropout(dropout)

def __call__(
    self,
    node_features: mx.array,
    edge_index: mx.array,
    edge_features: mx.array,
    batch_indices: Optional[mx.array] = None,
) -> mx.array:
    """Predicts the target properties of each molecule.

    The arguments are in PyG's order ``(x, edge_index, edge_attr, batch)``.

    Args:
        node_features: Atom features, of shape ``[num_atoms, in_channels]``.
        edge_index: Bonds, of shape ``[2, num_bonds]``.
        edge_features: Bond features, of shape ``[num_bonds, edge_dim]``.
        batch_indices: Molecule of each atom, of shape ``[num_atoms]``.
            Default: ``None`` (a single molecule).

    Returns:
        The predictions, of shape ``[num_molecules, out_channels]``.
    """
    if batch_indices is None:
        batch_indices = mx.zeros(node_features.shape[0], dtype=mx.int32)

    # Atom embedding
    x = nn.leaky_relu(self.lin1(node_features))
    h = nn.elu(self.gate_conv(edge_index, x, edge_features))
    h = self.dropout(h)
    x = nn.relu(self.gru(h, x))

    for conv, gru in zip(self.atom_convs, self.atom_grus):
        h = nn.elu(conv(edge_index, x))
        h = self.dropout(h)
        x = nn.relu(gru(h, x))

    # Molecule embedding: attention from the atoms to their molecule
    num_graphs = int(batch_indices.max().item()) + 1
    atoms = mx.arange(batch_indices.shape[0], dtype=batch_indices.dtype)
    mol_edge_index = mx.stack([atoms, batch_indices], axis=0)

    out = nn.relu(global_add_pool(x, batch_indices, num_graphs))
    for _ in range(self.num_timesteps):
        h = nn.elu(self.mol_conv(mol_edge_index, (x, out)))
        h = self.dropout(h)
        out = nn.relu(self.mol_gru(h, out))

    # Predictor
    out = self.dropout(out)
    return self.lin2(out)

def __init__(
    self,
    node_features_dim: Union[int, Tuple[int, int]],
    hidden_features_dim: int,
    num_layers: int,
    out_features_dim: Optional[int] = None,
    dropout: float = 0.0,
    act: Activation = "relu",
    norm: Normalization = None,
    jk: Optional[Literal["cat", "max", "lstm"]] = None,
    **kwargs: Any,
):
    super().__init__()
    if num_layers < 1:
        raise ValueError("`num_layers` must be at least 1")

    self.node_features_dim = node_features_dim
    self.hidden_features_dim = hidden_features_dim
    self.num_layers = num_layers
    self.out_features_dim = (
        out_features_dim if out_features_dim is not None else hidden_features_dim
    )
    self.act = _resolve_activation(act)
    # Normalization name, for convolutions with inner MLPs (`init_conv`).
    self._norm_name = norm
    self.dropout = nn.Dropout(dropout) if dropout > 0.0 else None
    self._dropout_p = dropout

    # Without Jumping Knowledge the last convolution maps directly to the
    # output size; with it, every convolution outputs hidden embeddings and
    # a final linear layer produces the output.
    conv_out_last = hidden_features_dim
    if out_features_dim is not None and jk is None:
        conv_out_last = out_features_dim
    self._plain_last = out_features_dim is not None and jk is None

    # As in PyG, a (src, dst) input size gives every layer separate
    # source and destination sizes.
    hidden_in: Union[int, Tuple[int, int]] = hidden_features_dim
    if isinstance(node_features_dim, (tuple, list)):
        node_features_dim = tuple(node_features_dim)
        hidden_in = (hidden_features_dim, hidden_features_dim)
    in_dims = [node_features_dim] + [hidden_in] * (num_layers - 1)
    out_dims = [hidden_features_dim] * (num_layers - 1) + [conv_out_last]
    self.convs = [
        self.init_conv(in_dim, out_dim, is_last=(i == num_layers - 1), **kwargs)
        for i, (in_dim, out_dim) in enumerate(zip(in_dims, out_dims))
    ]

    num_post = num_layers - 1 if self._plain_last else num_layers
    if norm is not None:
        self.norms = [
            _make_norm(norm, hidden_features_dim) for _ in range(num_post)
        ]

    if jk is not None:
        self.jk = JumpingKnowledge(jk, hidden_features_dim, num_layers)
        jk_dim = hidden_features_dim * (num_layers if jk == "cat" else 1)
        if out_features_dim is not None or jk == "cat":
            self.lin = Linear(jk_dim, self.out_features_dim)

def __call__(
    self,
    edge_index: mx.array,
    node_features: mx.array,
    edge_weights: Optional[mx.array] = None,
    edge_features: Optional[mx.array] = None,
) -> mx.array:
    """Computes the node embeddings (or predictions).

    Args:
        edge_index: Input edge index of shape `[2, num_edges]`
        node_features: Input node features
        edge_weights: Optional weight of each edge, for models whose
            convolution supports it.
        edge_features: Optional features of each edge, for models whose
            convolution supports it.

    Returns:
        An array of shape ``[num_nodes, out_features_dim]``.
    """
    conv_kwargs = {}
    if edge_weights is not None:
        if not self.supports_edge_weights:
            raise ValueError(
                f"{type(self).__name__} does not support `edge_weights`"
            )
        conv_kwargs["edge_weights"] = edge_weights
    if edge_features is not None:
        if not self.supports_edge_features:
            raise ValueError(
                f"{type(self).__name__} does not support `edge_features`"
            )
        conv_kwargs["edge_features"] = edge_features

    x = node_features
    xs = []
    for i, conv in enumerate(self.convs):
        x = conv(edge_index, x, **conv_kwargs)
        if not (self._plain_last and i == self.num_layers - 1):
            if "norms" in self:
                x = self.norms[i](x)
            if self.act is not None:
                x = self.act(x)
            if self.dropout is not None:
                x = self.dropout(x)
        xs.append(x)

    if "jk" in self:
        x = self.jk(xs)
    if "lin" in self:
        x = self.lin(x)
    return x

Bases: Module

Applies batch normalization over a batch of features as described in the Batch Normalization: Accelerating Deep Network Training by Reducing Internal Covariate Shift" paper.

\[ \mathbf{x}^{\prime}_i = \frac{\mathbf{x} - \textrm{E}[\mathbf{x}]}{\sqrt{\textrm{Var}[\mathbf{x}] + \epsilon}} \odot \gamma + \beta \]

The mean and standard-deviation are calculated per-dimension over all nodes inside the mini-batch.

Size of each input sample.

required eps

A value added to the denominator for numerical stability. (default: 1e-5)

required momentum

The value used for the running mean and running variance computation. (default: 0.1)

required affine

If set to True, this module has learnable affine parameters \(\gamma\) and \(\beta\). (default: True)

required track_running_stats

If set to True, this module tracks the running mean and variance, and when set to False, this module does not track such statistics and always uses batch statistics in both training and eval modes. (default: True)

required allow_single_element

If set to True, batches with only a single element will work as during in evaluation. That is the running mean and variance will be used. Requires track_running_stats=True. (default: False)

def __init__(
    self,
    num_features: int,
    eps: float = 1e-5,
    momentum: float = 0.1,
    affine: bool = True,
    track_running_stats: bool = True,
    allow_single_element: bool = False,
):
    super().__init__()
    if allow_single_element and not track_running_stats:
        raise ValueError(
            "'allow_single_element' requires "
            "'track_running_stats' to be set to `True`"
        )

    self.module = nn.BatchNorm(
        num_features=num_features,
        eps=eps,
        momentum=momentum,
        affine=affine,
        track_running_stats=track_running_stats,
    )
    self.num_features = num_features
    self.allow_single_element = allow_single_element
